`docs/rql.md`:

```md
# RQL in Godot-MCP

The data layer of the editor tools is RQL (Reflection Query Language, the NuGet package
[`com.IvanMurzak.Rql`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/com.IvanMurzak.Rql)): one query language instead of one tool
per operation, the same one Unity-MCP 1.0 uses. McpPlugin and its tool plumbing are unchanged; ReflectorNet stays the
data layer of the in-game runtime (`GodotMcpRuntime`) and of the editor's `Json` tool format.

RQL is licensed under the [PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0](https://polyformproject.org/licenses/shield/1.0.0/): free
to use, including in commercial products, except to provide a product that competes with the licensor's products.
The addon itself stays Apache-2.0.

## Tools

| Before (≤ 0.28) | Now |
|---|---|
| `node-find`, `node-get-data` | `rql-query` on `nodes` / `root` / `selection`: `nodes \| where class == "OmniLight3D" \| select $ref name path props["light_energy"]` |
| `node-modify` | `rql-mutate` `set`: C# members (`Position`, `Visible`, …) and every Godot property in `props["snake_name"]` (GDScript variables and GDExtension properties included) |
| `node-create`, `node-duplicate`, `node-delete`, `node-set-parent`, `node-reorder` | node calls `AddChild(class, name)`, `InstantiateScene(path)`, `Duplicate()`, `Free()`, `Reparent(node)`, `MoveChild(index)`; bulk create: `range(0, N) \| call editor.CreateNode(class, {name, parent, position, <Godot property>…})` and `[…] \| call editor.InstantiateScene(path, {…})` (once per item, every item checked first, one undo step, one receipt row with the node's `$ref` per item) |
| `scene-create`, `scene-open`, `scene-save`, `scene-list-opened`, `scene-get-data` | `editor \| call NewScene / OpenScene / SaveScene / SaveAllScenes`, the `scenes` source (`call Open / Save`), `root \| recurse children` |
| `resource-find`, `resource-get-data`, `resource-modify` | `godot.resources("Texture2D", "res://art")`, `godot.resource("res://…")` + `set` (the file is saved) |
| `resource-create`, `resource-move`, `resource-delete` | `editor \| call CreateResource / MoveResource / DeleteResource` (`.import` / `.uid` sidecars follow the file) |
| `filesystem-list`, `filesystem-reimport` | the `files` source (`path name dir ext type uid`), `editor \| call Reimport(files?)`, `CreateFolder` |
| — | on request: `files` members `deps` (what a file loads), `missingDeps` (broken references), `usedBy` (the saved scenes / resources that load it) and `importSettings["option"]` (the `.import` [params]; a write re-imports the file); node member `overrides` (how a scene instance differs from its scene file); `editor` members `undoHistory` / `redoHistory`; a Godot array property lists the values it holds (read-only: assign the whole list) |
| `editor-application-get-state` / `-set-state` | `editor` members `isPlaying` (writable), `playingScene`, `editedScene`, `godotVersion`; `call PlayScene / StopScene`; what the game run from the editor prints and its errors: the `gameLog` source (`Sequence LogType Message StackTrace`, read from the game's log file, `debug/file_logging/log_path`) |
| — | `editor \| call Undo()` / `Redo()`: the editor's own Undo / Redo (the Scene menu items behind Ctrl+Z), returning the action (`undone: RQL: <query>`; an rql-mutate's undo action is named after its query); an error when there is nothing to undo / redo |
| — | `editor \| call ReloadScene(path?)` (Scene → Reload Saved Scene: unsaved changes dropped), `NewScene(path, "res://base.tscn", name?)` (an inherited scene of a base scene) |
| `editor-selection-get` / `-set` | `editor` member `selection` (writable), the `selection` source |
| `console-get-logs`, `console-clear-logs` (editor) | the `console` source (`where LogType == "Error"`, `Sequence > N`; the framework's echo of each tool call is printed to the Output but not captured, and a plugin error is captured once), `editor \| call ClearConsole()` |
| `reflection-method-find`, `reflection-method-call` (editor) | `call CallMethod("name", [args])` on any Godot object, node / resource calls, `rql-schema` |
| — | `rql-schema`: sources, functions, the node classes in the edited scene; one type's members, methods and Godot properties (ClassDB) |

## Data models beyond nodes and resources

What the Godot editor keeps outside plain properties, each with read, write, undo and saving:

| Model | Read | Change | Saved to |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Groups** | node `groups` (persistent groups, internal `_…` excluded; a group a tool script joined without `persistent` is not listed), `godot.group("enemies")`, the `groups` source (`name nodes count global description`) | `call AddToGroup(g)` / `RemoveFromGroup(g)` (return whether anything changed), `set groups = [...]` (a listed edit-time group becomes persistent) | the scene (`groups=[…]` in the node header) |
| **Signals** | node `signals` (`name args connections`), `connections` (persistent ones: `signal target method flags deferred oneShot`), `incoming` | `call Connect(signal, target, method, deferred?, oneShot?)` (the method must exist in the target's script or class), `Disconnect(signal, target, method)`, a connection row's `Disconnect()` | the scene (`[connection …]`) |
| **Project settings** | the `settings` source (`name section value type changed`), `project` (`settings["section/key"]`, `name`, `mainScene`) | `project \| set settings["display/window/size/viewport_width"] = 1280` (typed like the Project Settings dialog), `call SetSetting(name, value)` (custom), `ClearSetting(name)` | `project.godot` |
| **Input map** | the `inputActions` source (`name events deadzone builtIn`); events as text: `Key:Space`, `Key:Ctrl+S`, `PhysicalKey:W`, `Mouse:Left`, `Mouse:Shift+WheelUp`, `JoypadButton:A`, `JoypadMotion:LeftX-` | `project \| call AddInputAction(name, events?, deadzone?)` / `RemoveInputAction` / `AddInputEvent` / `RemoveInputEvent`; rows: `call AddEvent / RemoveEvent / Remove`, `set events = [...]`, `set deadzone` | `project.godot` (`[input]`, all devices) |
| **Autoloads** | the `autoloads` source (`name path singleton order`) | `project \| call AddAutoload(name, path, singleton?)` / `RemoveAutoload`; rows: `set path`, `set singleton`, `call Remove()` | `project.godot` (`[autoload]`) |
| **Global groups** | the `groups` source (`global`, `description`) | `project \| call AddGlobalGroup(name, description?)` / `RemoveGlobalGroup` | `project.godot` (`[global_group]`) |
| **TileSet** | `sources` (`id kind atlas scenes texture tileCount`), `physicsLayers`, `navigationLayers`, `occlusionLayers`, `terrainSets` (`index mode terrains`), `customDataLayers` (`index name type`); an atlas source's `tiles` (`coords size alternatives data`) and `gridSize` | `call AddAtlasSource(texture, tileSize?)`, `RemoveSource(id)`, `AddPhysicsLayer()`, `AddNavigationLayer()`, `AddOcclusionLayer()`, `AddTerrainSet(mode?)`, `AddTerrain(set, name, color?)`, `AddCustomDataLayer(name, type)`; atlas: `CreateTile(coords, size?)`, `RemoveTile(coords)`, `CreateTilesFromTexture()`; tile settings on `data` (TileData: `Modulate`, `ZIndex`, `props["custom_data_0"]` …); layer settings in `props["physics_layer_0/collision_layer"]` | its `.tres` (or the scene that embeds it) |
| **Theme** | `types`, `items` (`type kind name value`), maps keyed `"ControlType/item"`: `colors`, `constants`, `fonts`, `fontSizes`, `icons`, `styleboxes` | `set colors["Button/font_color"] = "#ffcc00"` (a new key adds the item, `null` removes it), `call ClearItem(kind, key)`, `ClearType(type)` | its `.tres` |
| **Shader parameters** | ShaderMaterial `uniforms` (`name type group default value overridden`; defaults from the rendering server, else the literal in the code — the headless renderer keeps none), `params["uniform"]`; a Shader's (or VisualShader's) `uniforms` | `set params["speed"] = 2, params["tint"] = "#3388ff"` (typed by the uniform, validated against the shader's uniform list, a sampler takes a texture of its class), `null` or `call ClearParam(name)` reverts to the default, `ClearParams()` | the material's `.tres` (`shader_parameter/…`) |
| **Layer names** | the `layers` source (`kind index bit name setting` for 2d/3d render, physics, navigation and avoidance); every object's `layerNames["<property>"]` for its layer-hinted properties (`collision_layer`, `collision_mask`, `visibility_layer`, `light_mask`, `layers`, `cull_mask`, `navigation_layers`, a TileSet's `physics_layer_0/collision_mask` …) as a list of names, an unnamed layer as its number | rows: `set name = "enemies"`; objects: `set layerNames["collision_mask"] = ["world", 3]` (names or numbers; bits above the kind's count are kept); the raw ints (`CollisionMask`, `props["collision_mask"]`) keep working | `project.godot` (`[layer_names]`); the scene / resource |
| **MeshLibrary** | `items` (`id name mesh meshTransform shapes navigationMesh navigationMeshTransform navigationLayers preview`), an item's `shapes` (`index shape transform`) | `call CreateItem(name, mesh?, id?)`, `RemoveItem(id)` (a removed item comes back with all its settings on undo); rows: `set name / mesh / meshTransform / navigationMesh / navigationLayers / preview …`, `call AddShape(shape, transform?)`, `ClearShapes()` | its `.tres` |
| **Plane** | `"(a, b, c, d)"` — normal and distance (e.g. `WorldBoundaryShape3D.Plane`) | text, list or object literal | — |
| **Projection** | 16 numbers column by column (e.g. a `mat4` uniform) | text or list | — |
| **RID** | `"RID(1234)"`, `Id`, `IsValid` (a World3D's `Space`, `Texture2DRD.TextureRdRid` …) | read-only: an opaque server handle | — |
| **Callable** | `"Player::_on_hit"` (`target::method`; the target as a node path, a `res://` path or `Class#id`), `target`, `method`, `valid` | that text, `[target, method]`, `{target: …, method: …}` or `godot.callable(target, method)`; the target must have the method (e.g. `MultiplayerSpawner.SpawnFunction`, a `CallMethod` argument) | — (a Callable property is not stored) |

Structural changes register their own do/undo operations (connect/disconnect, add/remove group, add/remove a TileSet
source, layer or tile — a removed tile comes back with its data — Theme items and MeshLibrary items); shader parameters,
layer masks and MeshLibrary item settings are stored properties and go through the property snapshot; project settings are snapshotted
like any object, and undoing them writes `project.godot` again. Changes to a sub-resource stored inside a resource
file (a TileSet's atlas source, also one created in the same session) save that file.

Kept as tools: `script-*`, `screenshot-*`, `ping`, `godot-skill-*`, `runtime-errors-*`. The **in-game runtime** tool
surface is unchanged: `console-*`, `reflection-*`, `runtime-errors-*` and `ping` stay registered in a game build (the
editor removes `console-*` / `reflection-*` from the plugin it builds — `RqlInstaller.EditorReplacedTools`).

With the default `toolFormat` `Rql` (config key `toolFormat`, env `GODOT_MCP_TOOL_FORMAT`), the other tools take RQL
values as arguments (`"Level/Player"`, `ref("Node3D#12")`, `godot.find("Name")` for a `NodeRef`) and return compact
text; `Json` keeps ReflectorNet's JSON schemas and structured results. `toolTextEscaping` (`Minimal` / `Ascii` /
`Json`) controls how quoted text in those results is escaped.

## Writes: undo and saving

- **All-or-nothing.** Every target and value is checked before anything is written; a failure changes nothing.
  `dry_run: true` returns the receipt (`$ref member old new`) without changing anything. The receipt leaves out
  assignments that found the value already set; they are counted (`N unchanged assignment(s) not listed`).
- **Target limit.** A `set` / `call` stage changes at most 200 objects by default; `max_targets` (1–1000) raises it for
  an intended bulk change, which stays one all-or-nothing call and one undo action (`RqlTargetLimit`). Omitted (or 200), no
  budget is sent (the default applies); a value outside 1–1000 is refused by RQL (`invalid-value`) before anything runs. A misspelt member
  that leaves a mutation with no target is an `unknown-member` error; a member some Godot type declares (a polymorphic
  `nodes` stream with no node of that type) stays a warning (`RqlGodot.Names.cs`, the engine's `IsKnownMember`, which
  adds the members of the engine's registered `Adapters`).
- **Godot names.** `$type`, `$ref`, schemas and hints show Godot's class names (`GPUParticles3D`, `CSGBox3D`, `Object`),
  taken from the C# binding's `[GodotClassName]` (the engine's `TypeDisplayName`); `is` and `ref()` accept the C# names
  too. Hints name the tools: `rql-schema` (`SchemaHint`) and `rql-mutate` (`MutateHint`).
- **Undo.** One `EditorUndoRedoManager` action per `rql-mutate` (Ctrl+Z): a `set` snapshots the stored Godot properties
  of every changed object and records the differences as do/undo properties. The changed object is the nearest node,
  resource or project-settings object enclosing the write; a plain `Object` held by a node property is snapshotted
  itself, one beneath a view row is a change of the object the row stands for (a tile's `TileData` → its atlas
  source). Undo steps a setter registers itself (Theme items, `groups`) join the action only when the `set` commits:
  a `set` the engine rolls back leaves no undo entry (`RqlSetStageBuffer`). The structural node calls register the
  same do/undo methods the Scene dock does (the removed node of `Free()` stays alive in the undo history). An action
  that touches scene nodes and global objects (file resources, project settings) is split in two, one per undo
  history; every step is forced into its action's history (`ForceFixedHistory`), so a path-less resource cannot
  scatter it.
- **Saving** follows the replaced tools: a change to a node of the edited scene marks the scene unsaved — write it
  with `editor | call SaveScene()` (like Ctrl+S; `node-modify` did not save either); a change to a resource stored in
  its own file (`res://….tres`) is saved to that file after the mutation, like `resource-modify` (only when a property
  actually changed), and undo / redo of that change save the file again. Built-in (scene-embedded) resources mark the
  scene unsaved. Problems saving become `not-saved` warnings on the receipt. A file written into a folder the editor
  filesystem never scanned (`NewScene`, `CreateResource`, `SaveScene(path)`, `CreateFolder`, `script-create`) triggers a
  full scan after the write (`RqlReimport.Register`): `UpdateFile` ignores such a file, so the `files` source,
  `godot.resources(type, folder)` and a new GDScript `class_name` would not see it (a second such file in the same
  frame is registered when that scan lands; a `.gdignore` or dot-named folder is never scanned for). `NewScene` onto the path of a scene
  that is still open in a background tab (its file was deleted while another scene was edited) replaces the cached
  scene and reloads that tab, so the new scene is shown, not the old nodes; `OpenScene` fails when the editor ends up
  on another scene than the one asked for.
- **Refused instead of silently changed**: a rename Godot would alter (a character it does not allow in node names,
  `. : @ / " %`, or a sibling's name); `SaveScene(path)` onto another existing file; `InstantiateScene` of a scene that
  contains the edited one; `MoveResource` that changes the extension; `DeleteResource` of a file a scene or resource still
  uses, the edited scene's unsaved nodes included (`DeleteResource(path, true)` deletes anyway); moving or deleting
  `res://project.godot`, `res://.godot/` or this addon; `CallMethod` on a method of a non-`@tool` script (it does not run
  in the editor), with the wrong number of arguments or with an argument that does not convert to the type the method
  declares; a multi-target `Connect` where one target lacks the signal or method; `Free`, `Reparent`, `MoveChild`,
  `Duplicate` or a rename of a node that belongs to a scene instance (Godot saves only property overrides of those; the
  Scene dock refuses the same edits). Paths stay inside the edited scene: the root's `parent` is null and
  `godot.find("..")` finds nothing (a miss suggests similar node paths).
- **Batch checks** (RQL `MutationPolicy.ValidateBatch`, run on every `set` / `call` stage before anything changes, dry
  runs included; a refusal is `invalid-value`): a `Free()` of a node inside a scene instance is refused up front unless
  an ancestor is freed by the same call (`godot.find("Enemy") | recurse children | call Free()` removes the instance with
  its nodes). Hints never advise `budgets.*` (the tools take no budgets) and a `ref("Name")` hint names `godot.find("…")`.
- **Targets and map entries**: `$index` / `$path` in a `set` value or `call` argument are the
  target's (`nodes | where name starts-with "Enemy" | sort name | set Position.X = $index * 2`); a `set` on the entries
  `get` streams from a map writes through it (`godot.resource("res://ui/theme.tres") | get colors | where Key
  starts-with "Button/" | set Value = "#ffffff"` is the key-path write `colors["Button/…"]`, undo and save included).
- **Scene instances**: `InstantiateScene` instances like the Scene dock (`GenEditState.Instance`), so the `.tscn` stores only
  the overrides and the instance keeps following its scene file (type, script, groups). A change to a node inside an
  instance (a property, a group, a child added to it) turns on that instance's Editable Children, undoably, because Godot
  saves changes inside an instance only then.
- **Values as an agent writes them**: `CallMethod` converts each argument like a `set` to the type the Godot method
  declares (`"(0, 5)"` for a Vector2i, `"res://…"` for a resource, an enum by name:
  `CallMethod("set_anchors_preset", ["FullRect"])`); an enum-hinted int property takes its inspector label
  (`props["grow_horizontal"] = "Both"`), its number, or (Godot 4.4+) its setter's enum constant (`"GROW_DIRECTION_BOTH"`); an object literal
  naming a class builds a new embedded resource: `set Shape = {"$type": "BoxShape3D", Size: "(1, 2, 1)"}` (or
  `{class: "BoxShape3D", …}`; a class Godot cannot instantiate is refused). Script classes (GDScript `class_name`) work in
  those literals, in `CreateResource(path, "ItemData")` and in `godot.resources("ItemData")`.
- **Rotation is radians** (`Rotation`, `GlobalRotation` of Node3D, Node2D, Control): a written angle beyond a full turn
  (`set Rotation = "(-45, 30, 0)"`) is applied as given, and the receipt warns (`radians`) with the `RotationDegrees` write that
  was probably meant. Script-only Godot properties (usage none, such as `rotation_degrees`, `global_position`) are reachable
  by name in `props["…"]` (not listed among its keys). An enum-hinted int also takes its label without the note
  (`"PSSM 4 Splits"` for `"PSSM 4 Splits (Quality)"`) and (Godot 4.4+) its C# enum name (`"Parallel4Splits"`).
- **Printed structs** are tidied for reading (components below 1e-6 print as 0, at most 7 significant digits, no
  exponent): float noise such as `-4.371139E-08` in a rotated basis never reaches the agent; comparisons and stored values
  stay exact. An object literal compares like the text form: `where Position == {x: 0, y: 1, z: 0}`.

## Code

- `addons/godot_mcp/Editor/Rql/` (namespace `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Editor.Rql`):
  - `RqlGodot*.cs` — the engine over the live editor: factory (`AccessorMode.Compiled`, `$ref` = `Class#instance id`
    via `GodotObject.InstanceFromId`, liveness via `IsInstanceValid`), sources and functions, mutation hooks, node
    operations. One engine per editor session; `Reset()` on plugin teardown.
  - `EditorApi/` — the `editor` source (state, scenes, resource files, files, console, classes) and its view types.
  - `Adapters/` — one adapter per file: GodotObject (`id`, `class`, `props`, `CallMethod`), Node, Node2D, Node3D,
    Control, Resource, ProjectSettings (the `project` source), TileSet, TileSetAtlasSource, Theme, Shader, ShaderMaterial
    (`ShaderUniformDefaults.cs`: the pure parser of literal uniform defaults, unit-tested), MeshLibrary; StringName /
    NodePath / Variant / Callable (`CallableText.cs`: the pure text form, unit-tested); Vector2/3/4(I), Color, Quaternion,
    Basis, Transform2D/3D, Rect2(I), Aabb, Plane, Projection, Rid (pure C#, unit-tested; `-0` prints as `0`); NodeRef (tool
    arguments).
  - `RqlGodot.Signals.cs` — groups and signal connections of the edited scene's nodes.
  - `RqlReferences.cs` — who still uses a file (saved scenes and resources, the edited scene's live nodes): `DeleteResource`'s check.
  - `RqlSetStageBuffer.cs`, `RqlMutationOwner.cs` — the mutation hooks' pure parts (setter undo steps held until their
    `set` commits; which object a change is snapshotted on), unit-tested.
  - `Settings/` — project settings, input map (`InputEventText.cs`: the pure event grammar, unit-tested;
    `InputEvents.cs`: ⇄ Godot `InputEvent`s), autoloads and groups (`RqlProject.cs`), layer names (`LayerNames.cs`: the pure
    mask ⇄ name mapping, unit-tested; `RqlLayers.cs`: the `layers` source and the `layerNames` map).
  - `Modules/TestHooksModule.cs` — `test.undo` / `test.redo` / `test.action` / `test.undoManager` (true only when the
    undo manager is reachable; the smoke's probe) / `test.addToGroup(node, group, persistent)`, only with
    `GODOT_MCP_RQL_TEST_HOOKS=1` (the live smoke drives undo with them; never on in a user's editor).
  - `Modules/GodotCoreModule.cs`, `Modules/ToolTypesModule.cs` — the core module; modules are discovered in every loaded
    assembly (`GodotAssemblyUtils.AllAssemblies`), so an extension's `IRqlModule` in the consumer project assembly is
    found as soon as it is installed (its `ctx.AddGuide` text appears in the `godot-rql` skill).
  - `RqlGodotSchema.cs`, `GodotTypes.cs`, `RqlGuide.cs` (agent texts; every example runs in CI), `Skill_Rql.cs`
    (`godot-rql`), `ToolFormat/` (`RqlToolBinding`, McpPlugin `IToolBinding`), `RqlInstaller.cs`, `RqlReimport.cs`.
- `addons/godot_mcp/Editor/Tools/Tool_Rql*.cs` — the three tools.
- Installation: `GodotMcpPlugin` calls `RqlInstaller.Install` and hands the configuration it returns to the
  `GodotMcpConnection` constructor (`configurePlugin`), which invokes it after building each plugin.

## Hot reload

The RQL assemblies are NuGet dependencies, which the addon's resolver loads into the default (non-collectible) load
context. RQL keeps process-wide caches keyed by `Type` / `MemberInfo`; once a query touched a type of the collectible
project assembly they would keep it alive and a C# rebuild could not unload it. Teardown therefore drops the engine,
the tool signatures and the type index, and `RqlStaticCaches.Clear()` empties those caches by reflection (RQL 0.1 has
no public API for it; the xUnit suite fails if the fields it clears disappear). Module and type discovery skip the
previous copy of the project assembly that the process may still list during a reload. The dock-reload CI legs prove
the reload still unloads.

## Tests

- `Godot-MCP.Tests/Rql*Tests.cs` (xUnit, no Godot binary): every guide example parses, the struct adapters (Plane,
  Projection, Rid and negative zero included), the input-event text grammar, layer names ⇄ bits, shader uniform defaults,
  the Callable text form, the tool binding (schemas, RQL arguments, compact results, escaping), type names, the cache
  release, the config setting, and the mutation hooks' pure parts over a real engine (a rolled-back `set` drops its
  setters' undo steps, calls keep theirs; owner selection).
- `scripts/smoke_rql.py` (CI: `test_godot_runtime_harness.yml`, every Godot version of the matrix) against a live
  headless editor: read-back of every change from the `.tscn` / `.tres` Godot wrote (the former
  `smoke_property_patches.py` cases), `AddChild` + `SaveScene` round-trip, resource move / delete with sidecars, and
  every example of the guide (`Godot-Tests/rql-guide-examples.json`) in order. `scripts/smoke_rql_models.py` adds
  ~500 checks: every existing adapter on real properties (Node2D, Node3D, Control, Resource, NodePath, StringName,
  Variant, NodeRef, the struct types), groups, signal connections, project settings, the input map, autoloads, global
  groups, TileSets and Themes — each change read back from the `.tscn` / `.tres` / `project.godot` Godot wrote,
  validation errors, dry runs, and (with `GODOT_MCP_RQL_TEST_HOOKS=1` in the editor) undo and redo of every kind of
  change; without the hooks (or without a reachable undo manager, probed by `test.undoManager()`) those checks print
  `SKIP` (CI passes `--require-test-hooks`, which fails instead).
  `scripts/smoke_rql_adapters.py` does the same for shader parameters (a text shader and a VisualShader), layer names,
  MeshLibrary items and the Projection / RID / Callable values. `scripts/smoke_rql_hazards.py` covers the edits that used
  to corrupt data or answer misleadingly (the refusals above, undo of a transform-keeping Reparent, undo of a resource
  file edit, object-literal compares, tidy struct text).
- `scripts/smoke_rql_agent.py` (run by `smoke_rql.py`): what agent runs could not do or got wrong — editor Undo / Redo, the
  radians warning, script-only props, enum labels, the sibling-rename hint, inherited scenes and ReloadScene, the `gameLog`
  of a game run from the editor (skipped where the runner cannot start the game).
- `scripts/smoke_rql_semantics.py` (run by `smoke_rql.py`): boolean conditions, Godot class names in `$type` / `$ref` /
  `is`, hints naming `rql-mutate`, group `items`, list equality, the `max_targets` range and `unchanged` receipts.
- The extension suite (`test_extensions.yml`, `scripts/extension_live.py`) runs every extension's live manifest in
  the default `Rql` format: each module's guide examples in order, read-backs, and rejected values (`expectFailure`).

## Extensions are RQL modules

The `extensions/Godot-AI-*` packages add no MCP tools. Each ships an `IRqlModule` (`Editor/Rql/<Feature>Module.cs`,
Order 100) that compiles into the consumer project assembly, where the core discovers it: adapters for the Godot types
it covers (validated members that replace C# properties, virtual members, methods), sources for state no node owns,
and a guide (`ctx.AddGuide`) that the `godot-rql` skill renders. A module uses only Godot, `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` and
the BCL — never core-addon types — so the package still builds on its own; undo, dirty marking and saving come from the
core's mutation hooks, which record the Godot object a `set` writes or a `call` targets. Extensions that wrap a
GDScript or GDExtension addon (Beehave, Dialogic, PhantomCamera, Terrain3D) cannot target its classes with an adapter
(they have no C# type), so they expose a source (`beehave`, `dialogic`, `phantomcamera`, `terrain3d`) with rows and
validated calls where the addon needs them, and otherwise write through `props["…"]` and the core node calls. Every guide
example is unit-tested to parse and runs live in the extension suite (`tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json`). The scaffold is
`templates/extension/` (`python scripts/new_extension.py <Feature>`); the Unity-MCP counterparts are its extensions'
`Editor/Scripts/Rql/*Module.cs`.

`docs/runtime-security.md`:

```md
# Runtime (in-game) security contract

Godot-MCP can run **inside a running / exported game build** (debug or release), not only the editor —
see [Runtime usage (in-game)](../README.md#runtime-usage-in-game) for the full how-to. Running an MCP
connection inside a shipped game opens a **remote-control surface**: anything your registered
`[AiToolType]` tools can do, a connected MCP client can drive. This document is the security contract
for that mode. Read it before shipping a build that calls `GodotMcpRuntime.Initialize(...)`.

## Guarantees the runtime gives you

- **Opt-in only — never auto-connects.** The editor plugin connects on boot; a game build does **not**.
  `GodotMcpRuntime.Initialize(...).Build()` returns a **default-OFF** `GodotMcpRuntimeHandle`. Nothing
  connects until *your* code explicitly calls `handle.Connect()`. There is no auto-connect code path in
  a non-editor build.
- **Zero tools by default — strictly manual.** A freshly-built runtime registers **no** MCP tools. The
  attack surface is exactly the set of `[AiToolType]` classes you opt in via
  `builder.WithToolsFromAssembly(...)` / `builder.WithTools(...)` — no more. With none registered, the
  connection still builds and connects with an empty tool set (exactly Unity-MCP's model).
- **Editor tool families cannot leak in.** The addon's 7 editor tool families (`Tool_Node`,
  `Tool_Scene`, `Tool_Resource`, `Tool_FileSystem`, `Tool_Script`, `Tool_Screenshot`, `Tool_Editor`)
  are gated by `#if TOOLS` and do **not compile** into an exported game build. Even a
  `WithToolsFromAssembly(...)` over the addon's own assembly cannot register them.
- **No persisted-config auto-load.** A game build never silently reads a saved (`user://`) config file —
  that is an editor-only convenience. Host and token come only from your code (`WithConfig`) or from
  `GODOT_MCP_*` process environment / a project `.env`, which `GodotMcpConfig` reads live.

## What you must do when enabling it

- **Connect deliberately.** Only call `handle.Connect()` when you actually intend to expose tools (a dev
  build, a QA harness, an explicitly-designed in-game agent feature). Call `handle.Disconnect()` /
  `handle.Dispose()` to stop exposing them.
- **Register the minimum tool set.** Prefer `WithTools(typeof(MyToolFamily))` over a broad
  `WithToolsFromAssembly(...)` when you only need a few tools. Every registered tool is reachable by a
  connected client.
- **Prefer loopback + a token.** For local tooling, bind Custom mode to a loopback host
  (`http://localhost:…` / `127.0.0.1`) and set `AuthOption = Consts.MCP.Server.AuthOption.token` with a real
  `Token`:

  ```csharp
  // using McpServerConsts = com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin.Common.Consts.MCP.Server;
  builder.WithConfig(config =>
  {
      config.ConnectionMode = GodotMcpConnectionMode.Custom;
      config.Host           = "http://localhost:8080";   // loopback
      config.AuthOption     = McpServerConsts.AuthOption.token;
      config.Token          = "your-secret-token";  // discouraged: see the env-var form below — don't ship a hard-coded secret
  });
  ```

  Prefer the out-of-band form below, so the build carries no embedded secret:

  ```bash
  export GODOT_MCP_CONNECTION_MODE=Custom
  export GODOT_MCP_HOST=http://localhost:8080
  export GODOT_MCP_AUTH_OPTION=token
  export GODOT_MCP_TOKEN=your-secret-token
  ```

- **Do not expose an unauthenticated MCP surface on a public interface in a release build** unless you
  have explicitly designed and secured that surface. Treat any non-loopback host as a deliberate,
  reviewed decision.
- **Change the host or mode only while disconnected.** Unless you assign your own `CredentialProvider`, each
  connection's bearer is bound to the mode and host it dials: after a change, a reconnect of the existing link
  is sent no token, so call `handle.Disconnect()` and `handle.Connect()` to switch servers.
- **Do not embed long-lived secrets in the shipped binary.** Prefer `GODOT_MCP_TOKEN` from the
  environment over a hard-coded `config.Token` so the token is not extractable from the build.
- **Enable runtime-error capture only on a trusted connection.** `builder.WithRuntimeErrorCapture()` is
  **OFF by default**. When enabled, captured errors forward the **full** message and (for C# faults) the
  **full managed stack trace** to the connected agent via the `runtime-errors-get` tool. Those strings can
  embed sensitive runtime data — absolute filesystem paths, machine/user names, query strings, or a
  secret/token that surfaced in an exception message or argument. That is the intended diagnostic value,
  but it widens the data exposed over the connection. Enable it only on a loopback host with
  `AuthOption = Consts.MCP.Server.AuthOption.token` and a real token — never on an unauthenticated public
  interface in a release build.

## In-game code execution (`WithScriptExecute`)

`builder.WithScriptExecute()` registers `script-execute` in the game: a connected client sends C#, the game
compiles it with Roslyn and runs it on its main thread. That is **arbitrary code execution in the game
process**, with the player's file system and network access. It is OFF by default and it needs a build
opt-in: an exported game has Code-Exec and Roslyn only when its `.csproj` sets `GodotMcpCodeExecInGame=true`
and defines `GODOT_MCP_CODE_EXEC_IN_GAME` (README "Running C# in the game"). Without the opt-in the call logs
a warning and registers nothing.

> **Games started from the editor.** Their build is the editor build (`TOOLS`), so the addon's editor tool
> families compile into the game assembly too. A `WithToolsFromAssembly(...)` over that assembly then
> registers them, the editor `script-execute` included, with or without `WithScriptExecute()`. In an export
> build they do not exist. Register specific types (`WithTools(...)`) if a game run from the editor must not
> offer them.

- **Debug / dev builds only.** Gate the call (and the csproj opt-in) behind your own dev switch. Never ship it
  enabled in a public release build.
- **Loopback + token, always.** Use a loopback host and `AuthOption = token` with a real token from the
  environment. Anyone who can call tools on the connection owns the process.
- **Desktop CoreCLR only.** NativeAOT and iOS cannot run code emitted at run time; mobile is untested.
- **Size.** The opt-in adds Roslyn (`Microsoft.CodeAnalysis*.dll`, several MB) to the export. RQL is never
  shipped.

## Environment variables

The runtime config (`GodotMcpConfig`) reads these `GODOT_MCP_*` variables live (process env or project
`.env`). They override values set in code at resolution time.

| Variable | Values | Description |
| -------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `GODOT_MCP_CONNECTION_MODE` | `Cloud` / `Custom` | Connection mode (a loopback host implies `Custom`). |
| `GODOT_MCP_CLOUD_URL` | URL | Override the Cloud base URL (default `https://ai-game.dev`). |
| `GODOT_MCP_HOST` | URL | Custom-mode server host (default `http://localhost:8080`). |
| `GODOT_MCP_AUTH_OPTION` | `none` / `oauth` / `token` | Custom-mode auth: anonymous / account (oauth) / offline bearer (`token`). |
| `GODOT_MCP_TOKEN` | string | The bearer token (routed to Cloud or Custom by the active mode). |
| `GODOT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL` | `Trace` / `Debug` / `Info` / `Warning` / `Error` / `None` | Log-verbosity threshold. |
| `GODOT_MCP_EDITOR_PID` | process id | Set by the editor plugin in the editor process, so every process the editor starts inherits it. While that editor runs, the runtime's `Connect()` stays offline in a process that carries it (unless opted in below). |
| `GODOT_MCP_RUNTIME_FROM_EDITOR` | `1` / `true` | Process env only. Lets the runtime connect in a game started from the Godot editor (default: it stays offline there, because the game inherits the editor's `GODOT_MCP_*` settings); same as `builder.ConnectWhenRunFromEditor()`. |

## Editor-side surfaces (accepted posture)

The contract above is for a **game build**. Two editor-side surfaces are documented here for completeness;
both are **by design** today (no encryption / no shared-secret is implemented yet — those are deferred,
parity-constrained decisions to coordinate across the Unity / Godot / Unreal siblings).

### Editor token storage is plaintext at rest

When you connect the **editor plugin** (Cloud device-auth, or a Custom-mode token), it persists your
connection config to **`user://godot-mcp-config.json`** (Godot resolves `user://` to the per-platform user
data directory via `ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath`). The bearer token (`token`) and Cloud token
(`cloudToken`) are written as **plaintext JSON** — they are **not** encrypted and **not** stored in an OS
keystore.

- **Trust assumption: the local user account.** Anyone who can read your user data directory can read the
  token. Treat `user://godot-mcp-config.json` as a secret — don't commit it, sync it to a shared drive, or
  paste it.
- **Rotation.** Clear the saved token in the dock (or delete the file) and reconnect.
- **Precedence.** A `GODOT_MCP_TOKEN` process-env / `.env` value always shadows the persisted token at
  resolution time and is **not** written back into this file — so a CI / shared machine can run without
  ever persisting a token to disk.

### The dev-control bridge is unauthenticated but gated OFF

A development-only inject/control HTTP bridge (`DevControlServer`) exists for driving the editor dock from
tests / a terminal. It is **unauthenticated**, but its security boundary is threefold:

1. **Editor-only.** It is compiled behind `#if TOOLS`, so it does not exist in an exported game build.
2. **Loopback-only.** It binds **`127.0.0.1`** exclusively — never a routable interface.
3. **Env-gated OFF.** It is constructed and started **only when `GODOT_MCP_DEV_CONTROL=1`** (exactly `1`).
   An unset / any-other value means the bridge never listens — a shipped addon, and any normal editor
   session, never opens the surface.

That env gate is **load-bearing**: it is the single thing standing between "dev scaffolding" and "an
unauthenticated control surface on the live dock". It is enforced by a pure-managed predicate
(`DevControlGate.IsEnabled`) with a unit test (`DevControlGateTests`) **and** a boot-time assertion at the
construction site (`DevControlGate.AssertEnabledOrThrow`), so a regression that wires the bridge on without
the env var fails fast in CI and at runtime rather than silently shipping enabled.

```

`extensions/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# extensions/

Optional Godot-MCP packages. Each `Godot-AI-<Feature>/` owns its source-only NuGet
package, version, license, xUnit tests and live manifest. Every extension is an RQL module
(`Editor/Rql/`, `IRqlModule`) with no MCP tools of its own; see `../docs/rql.md`.

- `manifest.json` — explicit module inventory; no automatic discovery of arbitrary folders.
- `Godot-AI-*/extension.json` — identity, source provenance and pinned test-addon metadata.
- `Godot-AI-*/src/` — package source and NuGet build props; no dependency on another extension.
- `Godot-AI-*/tests/` — xUnit projects and the live manifest (`e2e/e2e-tools.json`: every guide example; driver
  `../scripts/extension_e2e.py`).
- `Godot-AI-*/testbed/` — isolated consumer fixture; not the combined live project.
- `Shared/Tests/` — test sources every extension test project links (the guide checks); never packaged.

Never add module sources to the core assembly. Compilation of a consumer containing
core plus exactly one packed extension must succeed independently of the combined
live-editor test. A combined build alone cannot prove dependency isolation.

Keep package IDs and historical NuGet versions stable. Publish only selected changed
versions. GodotSharp and third-party addons must not enter package dependencies.
Shared tests and release commands are documented in `../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md`.

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# AGENTS.md — Godot-AI-Animation

A **Godot-MCP extension** for Godot's built-in animation system (`AnimationPlayer` / `AnimationTree`,
`AnimationLibrary`, `Animation`), shipped as an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools, only what the core
`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools need to build animations (library / animation maps, creation,
tracks and keys, validation, an agent guide rendered into the core `godot-rql` skill). A **source-only NuGet
package** (`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Animation`) compiled inside the consumer's Godot project against the
consumer's own GodotSharp; the packaging recipe is in `docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`.

## Layout

- `src/Godot-AI-Animation/Editor/Rql/` — the module:
  - `AnimationModule.cs` — the `IRqlModule` (Order 100, `#if TOOLS`): the three adapters and the guide.
  - `Godot_AnimationMixer_Adapter.cs` (AnimationPlayer + AnimationTree: `libraries`, `animations`, `AddLibrary`,
    `CreateAnimation`), `Godot_AnimationLibrary_Adapter.cs` (`animations`, `CreateAnimation`),
    `Godot_Animation_Adapter.cs` (`Length`, `tracks`, `trackCount`, `AddTrack`, `InsertKey`, `InsertTransformKey`)
    — one adapter per type (`#if TOOLS`); the Godot calls behind them live in `AnimationOps.cs`.
  - Pure-managed, NOT behind `#if TOOLS`: `AnimationRules.cs` (validation), `AnimationGuide.cs` (the guide),
    `AnimationTrackRow.cs` (the read-only `tracks` row), `AnimationTrackKind.cs` / `AnimationLoopMode.cs` (label
    parsers and Godot enum mapping).
- `src/Godot-AI-Animation/build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Animation.props` — source-injection props, auto-imported
  by NuGet in the consumer; MUST stay named `<PackageId>.props`.
- `tests/Godot-AI-Animation.Tests/` — xUnit (no Godot binary): rules, label parsers, guide examples parse, the
  module's member tables (GodotSharp metadata, `TOOLS` defined), and the e2e manifest runs every guide example.
- `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` — the live calls (`rql-*`), driven by `scripts/extension_e2e.py` from the monorepo suite.
- `testbed/Animation-Testbed.csproj` — consumer project restoring the local-packed package (injection proof).
- `commands/` — `bump-version`, `update-core`, `init` (`.ps1` + `.py`), `get-version.ps1`.
- CI and publishing are centralized in the monorepo; see `../../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md`.

## Critical invariants

- **RQL surface.** Everything is registered by `AnimationModule` and documented in `AnimationGuide` (topic
  "Animation"). Every guide example runs, in order, in `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` (xUnit-asserted).
- **Undo follows the call target.** The core snapshots the stored Godot properties of the object a call is made
  on. So a method lives on the object it changes: `AddLibrary` on the mixer (its `libraries`),
  `CreateAnimation` on the library, `AddTrack` / keys on the Animation. The mixer's `CreateAnimation` is undoable
  only when it adds the library (documented in the guide); keep that caveat if you change it.
- **Validate, never clamp.** Every call checks all its arguments (`AnimationRules`, the label parsers, existing
  names) before it changes anything, so Godot never logs an error (the headless suite fails on any `ERROR:`).
- The namespace ends in `.Animation`, which shadows `Godot.Animation`: use the `GodotAnimation` alias.
- The module uses only Godot, `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` and the BCL, never core-addon types (the authoring build has
  no core). Undo, dirty marking and saving come from the core's mutation hooks.

## Build / test (no Godot binary)

```bash
dotnet build src/Godot-AI-Animation/Godot-AI-Animation.csproj -c Debug   # the module (#if TOOLS included)
dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-Animation.Tests/Godot-AI-Animation.Tests.csproj
```

The live suite (one headless editor for every module) is `python scripts/test_extensions.py` from the monorepo
root. `dotnet pack` reuses the **global NuGet cache** for an already-cached version: when re-packing the same
`Version`, clear `~/.nuget/packages/com.ivanmurzak.godot.mcp.animation/<ver>` (or pack a unique version).

## Conventions

- Root namespace `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Animation`. Every `.cs` starts with the Apache-2.0 header and
  `#nullable enable`.
- The package declares only the `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin` / `ReflectorNet` / `Rql` pins (equal to the core's); **GodotSharp must
  never become a package dependency** (CI asserts the nuspec). Bump them with `commands/update-core.ps1`.

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/README.md`:

```md
# Animation Tools

RQL module for Godot AnimationPlayer: libraries, animations, tracks and keys for the core rql-query / rql-mutate tools, plus an agent guide.

Optional Godot-MCP extension, independently versioned as NuGet package `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Animation` (1.0.1).
Requires a Godot C# project (4.3.0+) with a core `godot_mcp` addon that has the RQL tools
(`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, the release after 0.28.0).

## Install

```sh
godot-cli install-plugin /path/to/project
godot-cli install-extension com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Animation /path/to/project
godot-cli build /path/to/project
```

The installer resolves the latest stable version from NuGet; use `--version 1.0.1` to request an exact version.
Packages contain C# source and build props, compiled against the project's own GodotSharp.
Previous NuGet versions remain installable after the repository migration.

## RQL

Since 1.0.0 the extension is an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools. Agents create players, libraries,
animations, tracks and keys with the core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools, and the module's guide
is part of the core `godot-rql` skill. The module adds:

- **AnimationPlayer / AnimationTree** (any `AnimationMixer`): the read-only maps `libraries["name"]` (`""` = the
  global library) and `animations["library/name"]`; calls `AddLibrary(name)` and
  `CreateAnimation(name, length = 1, loopMode = "none", library = "")` (adds the library when it is missing).
- **AnimationLibrary**: `animations["name"]` and `CreateAnimation(name, length = 1, loopMode = "none")`.
- **Animation**: a validated `Length` (at least 0.001 s), read-only `tracks` rows (`index kind path keyCount`) and
  `trackCount`; calls `AddTrack(kind, path)` (`value`, `position-3d`, `rotation-3d`, `scale-3d`; returns the
  index), `InsertKey(track, time, value)` for value tracks and `InsertTransformKey(track, time, "(x, y, z)")` for
  the 3D transform tracks (rotation as Euler degrees).

```
root | call AddChild("Node3D", "Mover")
root | call AddChild("AnimationPlayer", "Player")
nodes | where name == "Player" | call AddLibrary("")
nodes | where name == "Player" | get libraries[""] | call CreateAnimation("Idle", 2, "linear")
nodes | where name == "Player" | call CreateAnimation("Walk", 1, "none", "Extra")
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"] | call AddTrack("value", "Mover:position:x")
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"] | call InsertKey(0, 0.5, 1.5)
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"] | call AddTrack("rotation-3d", "Mover")
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"] | call InsertTransformKey(1, 1, "(0, 90, 0)")
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"] | set Length = 1.5, LoopMode = "Pingpong"
nodes | where name == "Player" | get animations["Idle"].tracks | select index kind path keyCount
nodes | where $ is AnimationPlayer | select name animations.keys() libraries.keys()
```

Every write is one undoable action (it changes the animation, library or player it is called on) and marks the
scene unsaved (`editor | call SaveScene()` writes it). One exception: `CreateAnimation` on the player into a
library that already exists changes only that library, so it is not undoable; call it on the library
(`get libraries["…"] | call CreateAnimation(…)`) instead. Invalid values (a length below 0.001, a negative key
time, a missing track, a name with `/`, `:`, `,` or `[`, an existing name) fail the call and change nothing
(0.x clamped lengths and key times).

### Migrating from 0.x

| 0.x tool | RQL |
| --- | --- |
| `animation-defaults` | removed: typical values (length 1 s, loop mode none) are the call defaults and in the guide |
| `animation-player-create` | `rql-mutate` `root \| call AddChild("AnimationPlayer", "Player")` |
| `animation-library-add` | `rql-mutate` `nodes \| where name == "Player" \| call AddLibrary("Extra")` |
| `animation-create` | `rql-mutate` `… \| get libraries[""] \| call CreateAnimation("Idle", 2, "linear")` or `… \| call CreateAnimation("Idle", 2, "linear", "")` on the player |
| `animation-add-track` | `rql-mutate` `… \| get animations["Idle"] \| call AddTrack("value", "Mover:position:x")` |
| `animation-insert-key` | `rql-mutate` `… \| get animations["Idle"] \| call InsertKey(0, 0.5, 1.5)`; transform tracks: `call InsertTransformKey(1, 1, "(0, 90, 0)")` |
| `animation-get` | `rql-query` `nodes \| where $ is AnimationPlayer \| select name animations.keys() libraries.keys()`; `… \| get animations["Idle"] \| select Length LoopMode tracks` |

## Development and releases

See the [monorepo test and release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md).
This module retains its own package, version, tests and Apache-2.0 [license](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/LICENSE).
Releasing another module does not rebuild or republish this package.

## Asset Library installation

The independent Asset Library entry is named **Godot MCP - Animation** and becomes public after moderator approval.
It downloads only this extension from its versioned GitHub release. Install Godot MCP core
and configure its NuGet dependencies first, then install the archive into the project and build C#.
The archive includes its own license, README and installation instructions. Third-party addon
prerequisites listed above still apply. Use either this source installation or this extension
NuGet package in a project; installing both creates duplicate C# types.

See the [Asset Library release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md#godot-asset-library).

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Set the extension package version (the single source of truth: the package csproj <Version>).

.DESCRIPTION
    Updates <Version> in the source-only package csproj under src/. The release workflow is version-gated
    on this value (it publishes only when <Version> increases AND the tag does not yet exist).

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/bump-version.ps1 -NewVersion "1.0.1"
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/bump-version.ps1 -NewVersion "1.0.1" -WhatIf
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$NewVersion,
    [switch]$WhatIf
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "../extension.json")) {
    $pythonCommand = Get-Command py, python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $pythonCommand) { throw "Python 3 is required for the central version helper." }
    $pythonArguments = @()
    if ($pythonCommand.Name -match '^py(\.exe)?$') { $pythonArguments += '-3' }
    $pythonArguments += @((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "bump-version.py"), $NewVersion)
    if ($WhatIf) { $pythonArguments += '--what-if' }
    & $pythonCommand.Source @pythonArguments
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

if ($NewVersion -notmatch '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z\.\-]+)?$') {
    throw "Invalid semantic version: '$NewVersion' (expected major.minor.patch[-prerelease])."
}

$RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$csproj = Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $RepoRoot "src") -Recurse -Filter *.csproj |
    Where-Object { (Get-Content $_.FullName -Raw) -match '<PackageId>' } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $csproj) { throw "Could not find the package csproj (with <PackageId>) under src/." }

$content = Get-Content $csproj.FullName -Raw
if ($content -notmatch '<Version>([^<]+)</Version>') { throw "No <Version> element in $($csproj.Name)." }
$current = $Matches[1]
$new = $content -replace '<Version>[^<]+</Version>', "<Version>$NewVersion</Version>"

Write-Host "Package: $($csproj.Name)"
Write-Host "Version: $current -> $NewVersion"
if ($WhatIf) { Write-Host "(WhatIf — no changes written)" -ForegroundColor Yellow; exit 0 }
Set-Content -Path $csproj.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline
Write-Host "Updated." -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Remember to commit, then push to main to trigger the version-gated release."

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/commands/bump-version.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Set the extension package version (the package csproj <Version>). POSIX/Python mirror of bump-version.ps1.

Usage:
  python commands/bump-version.py 1.0.1
  python commands/bump-version.py 1.0.1 --what-if
  python commands/bump-version.py --get        # print current version
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SEMVER = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.\-]+)?$")


def find_package_csproj(root: Path) -> Path:
    for p in (root / "src").rglob("*.csproj"):
        if "<PackageId>" in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
            return p
    raise SystemExit("error: could not find the package csproj (with <PackageId>) under src/")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("version", nargs="?", help="new semantic version, e.g. 1.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--what-if", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--get", action="store_true", help="print current version and exit")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    if (root / "extension.json").is_file():
        # Keep the monorepo inventory and package README versions in sync.
        sys.path.insert(0, str(root.parents[1] / "scripts"))
        from extension_release import bump
        from extensions import modules, SEMVER as stable_version
        module = modules(only=[root.name])[0]
        if args.get:
            print(module["version"])
            return 0
        if not args.version or not stable_version.fullmatch(args.version):
            ap.error("pass a stable major.minor.patch version")
        if args.what_if:
            print(f"{module['name']}: {module['version']} -> {args.version} (what-if)")
            return 0
        bump(module, args.version)
        return 0
    csproj = find_package_csproj(root)
    content = csproj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r"<Version>([^<]+)</Version>", content)
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"error: no <Version> element in {csproj.name}")
    current = m.group(1)

    if args.get:
        print(current)
        return 0

    if not args.version or not SEMVER.match(args.version):
        print("error: pass a semantic version major.minor.patch[-prerelease]", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    print(f"Package: {csproj.name}")
    print(f"Version: {current} -> {args.version}")
    if args.what_if:
        print("(what-if — no changes written)")
        return 0
    csproj.write_text(re.sub(r"<Version>[^<]+</Version>", f"<Version>{args.version}</Version>", content),
                       encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    print("Updated.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/commands/init.ps1`:

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Initialize a new Godot-MCP extension from this template: replace placeholders, rename files/folders,
    and activate the CI workflows.

.DESCRIPTION
    From a single -Feature name (PascalCase, e.g. "Particles") this derives and substitutes every
    placeholder, then renames any file/folder whose name contains YOUR_FEATURE, then activates CI by
    renaming `.github/workflows/*.yml-sample` -> `*.yml`.

    Derived values (override any with the matching parameter):
      Package id  : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>     (the NuGet <PackageId>)
      Repo        : IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-<Feature>          (-GitHubRepository)
      Display name: "<Feature> Tools"                       (-DisplayName)
      Description : "RQL module for Godot <Feature>."      (-Description)
      RQL source  : <feature-lowercased>                     (-SourceName; the module's RQL source name)

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/init.ps1 -Feature "Particles"

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/init.ps1 -Feature "Particles" -GitHubRepository "myuser/Godot-AI-Particles" -DisplayName "Particle Tools"
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)] [string]$Feature,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$DisplayName,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$Description,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$GitHubRepository,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$SourceName
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

if ($Feature -notmatch '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$') {
    throw "Feature must be alphanumeric PascalCase (letters/digits, starts with a letter). Got: '$Feature'"
}

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($DisplayName))      { $DisplayName = "$Feature Tools" }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Description))       { $Description = "RQL module for Godot $Feature." }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($GitHubRepository))  { $GitHubRepository = "IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-$Feature" }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($SourceName))        { $SourceName = $Feature.ToLower() }

$ScriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$RepoRoot  = Split-Path -Parent $ScriptDir

# Longest tokens first so no token is a prefix of another mid-replacement.
$Replacements = [ordered]@{
    "YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME_REPOSITORY" = $GitHubRepository
    "YOUR_DISPLAY_NAME"               = $DisplayName
    "YOUR_DESCRIPTION"                = $Description
    "YOUR_SOURCE"                     = $SourceName
    "YOUR_FEATURE"                    = $Feature
}

Write-Host "Initializing Godot-MCP extension:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Feature      : $Feature"
Write-Host "  Package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.$Feature"
Write-Host "  Repository   : $GitHubRepository"
Write-Host "  Display name : $DisplayName"
Write-Host "  RQL source   : $SourceName"
Write-Host ""

$ExcludeDirs = @('.git', 'bin', 'obj', '.godot', 'local-nuget', '.vs')

function Test-Excluded([string]$path) {
    foreach ($d in $ExcludeDirs) {
        if ($path -match "[\\/]$([regex]::Escape($d))([\\/]|$)") { return $true }
    }
    return $false
}

# 1) Replace placeholder content in all text files.
Write-Host "Replacing placeholders in file content..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$textExt = @('.cs','.csproj','.props','.targets','.md','.json','.yml','.yaml','.yml-sample','.godot','.config','.sh','.ps1','.py','.editorconfig','.gitignore','.txt')
Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoRoot -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object {
    $file = $_
    if (Test-Excluded $file.FullName) { return }
    if ($file.Name -eq 'init.ps1' -or $file.Name -eq 'init.py') { return }  # don't rewrite the running script
    $ext = $file.Extension.ToLower()
    $isText = ($textExt -contains $ext) -or ($file.Name -like '*.yml-sample') -or ($file.Name -eq 'LICENSE')
    if (-not $isText) { return }
    $content = Get-Content -Path $file.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($null -eq $content) { return }
    $new = $content
    foreach ($k in $Replacements.Keys) { $new = $new.Replace($k, $Replacements[$k]) }
    if ($new -ne $content) {
        Set-Content -Path $file.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline
        Write-Host "  updated $($file.FullName.Substring($RepoRoot.Length+1))" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    }
}

# 2) Rename files/folders whose NAME contains YOUR_FEATURE (deepest-first so children rename before parents).
Write-Host "Renaming files and folders..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoRoot -Recurse | Where-Object { -not (Test-Excluded $_.FullName) } |
    Sort-Object { $_.FullName.Length } -Descending | ForEach-Object {
        if ($_.Name -like '*YOUR_FEATURE*') {
            $newName = $_.Name.Replace('YOUR_FEATURE', $Feature)
            Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
            Write-Host "  renamed $($_.Name) -> $newName" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        }
    }

# 3) Activate CI: *.yml-sample -> *.yml
Write-Host "Activating CI workflows (*.yml-sample -> *.yml)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$wf = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".github/workflows"
if (Test-Path $wf) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $wf -Filter "*.yml-sample" | ForEach-Object {
        $target = $_.FullName -replace '\.yml-sample$', '.yml'
        Move-Item -Path $_.FullName -Destination $target -Force
        Write-Host "  activated $($_.Name) -> $([System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($target))" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Done. Next:" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  1. Review the changes, then build + test:"
Write-Host "       dotnet build src/Godot-AI-$Feature/Godot-AI-$Feature.csproj"
Write-Host "       dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-$Feature.Tests/Godot-AI-$Feature.Tests.csproj"
Write-Host "  2. Write the RQL module under src/Godot-AI-$Feature/Editor/Rql (adapters, sources, guide; see AGENTS.md)."
Write-Host "  3. Configure the NUGET_API_KEY secret, then push to main with a bumped <Version> to release."

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/commands/init.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Initialize a new Godot-MCP extension from this template (POSIX/Python path; mirrors init.ps1).

From a single --feature name (PascalCase, e.g. "Particles") this substitutes every placeholder, renames
files/folders whose name contains YOUR_FEATURE, then activates CI (*.yml-sample -> *.yml).

Derived (override with the matching flag):
  package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>
  repo         : IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-<Feature>      (--github-repository)
  display name : "<Feature> Tools"                   (--display-name)
  description  : "RQL module for Godot <Feature>."  (--description)
  RQL source   : <feature lowercased>                 (--source-name; the module's source, e.g. "particles | select …")

Usage:
  python commands/init.py --feature Particles
  python commands/init.py --feature Particles --github-repository myuser/Godot-AI-Particles
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXCLUDE_DIRS = {".git", "bin", "obj", ".godot", "local-nuget", ".vs"}
TEXT_EXT = {".cs", ".csproj", ".props", ".targets", ".md", ".json", ".yml", ".yaml",
            ".yml-sample", ".godot", ".config", ".sh", ".ps1", ".py", ".editorconfig",
            ".gitignore", ".txt"}
SELF = {"init.py", "init.ps1"}


def is_excluded(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
    rel_parts = path.relative_to(root).parts
    return any(part in EXCLUDE_DIRS for part in rel_parts)


def is_text(path: Path) -> bool:
    name = path.name
    if name == "LICENSE":
        return True
    if name.endswith(".yml-sample"):
        return True
    return path.suffix.lower() in TEXT_EXT


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Initialize a Godot-MCP extension from the template.")
    ap.add_argument("--feature", required=True, help="PascalCase feature name, e.g. Particles")
    ap.add_argument("--display-name")
    ap.add_argument("--description")
    ap.add_argument("--github-repository")
    ap.add_argument("--source-name")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    feature = args.feature
    if not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", feature):
        print(f"error: --feature must be alphanumeric PascalCase. Got: {feature!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    display = args.display_name or f"{feature} Tools"
    description = args.description or f"RQL module for Godot {feature}."
    repo = args.github_repository or f"IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-{feature}"
    source = args.source_name or feature.lower()

    # Longest tokens first so no token is a prefix of another mid-replacement.
    replacements = [
        ("YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME_REPOSITORY", repo),
        ("YOUR_DISPLAY_NAME", display),
        ("YOUR_DESCRIPTION", description),
        ("YOUR_SOURCE", source),
        ("YOUR_FEATURE", feature),
    ]

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

    print("Initializing Godot-MCP extension:")
    print(f"  Feature      : {feature}")
    print(f"  Package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.{feature}")
    print(f"  Repository   : {repo}")
    print(f"  Display name : {display}")
    print(f"  RQL source   : {source}\n")

    # 1) Replace placeholder content.
    print("Replacing placeholders in file content...")
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file() or is_excluded(path, root) or path.name in SELF or not is_text(path):
            continue
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        new = text
        for token, value in replacements:
            new = new.replace(token, value)
        if new != text:
            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
            print(f"  updated {path.relative_to(root)}")

    # 2) Rename files/folders containing YOUR_FEATURE, deepest-first.
    print("Renaming files and folders...")
    entries = [p for p in root.rglob("*") if not is_excluded(p, root)]
    for path in sorted(entries, key=lambda p: len(str(p)), reverse=True):
        if "YOUR_FEATURE" in path.name:
            new_name = path.name.replace("YOUR_FEATURE", feature)
            path.rename(path.with_name(new_name))
            print(f"  renamed {path.name} -> {new_name}")

    # 3) Activate CI.
    print("Activating CI workflows (*.yml-sample -> *.yml)...")
    wf = root / ".github" / "workflows"
    if wf.is_dir():
        for sample in wf.glob("*.yml-sample"):
            target = sample.with_name(sample.name[: -len("-sample")])
            sample.replace(target)
            print(f"  activated {sample.name} -> {target.name}")

    print("\nDone. Next:")
    print(f"  dotnet build src/Godot-AI-{feature}/Godot-AI-{feature}.csproj")
    print(f"  dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-{feature}.Tests/Godot-AI-{feature}.Tests.csproj")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/commands/update-core.ps1`:

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Update the core MCP / reflection / query pins (com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin / com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet /
    com.IvanMurzak.Rql) in lockstep across the package, tests, and testbed csproj files.

.DESCRIPTION
    These pins MUST equal the core Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP/Godot-MCP.csproj; scripts/extensions.py
    core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise); com.IvanMurzak.Rql is the RQL module API. When the core advances its pins,
    run this in the same change. Pass any of the three.

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -McpPlugin "6.11.0"
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -McpPlugin "6.11.0" -ReflectorNet "5.4.0" -WhatIf
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -Rql "0.2.0"
#>
param(
    [string]$McpPlugin,
    [string]$ReflectorNet,
    [string]$Rql,
    [switch]$WhatIf
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
if (-not $McpPlugin -and -not $ReflectorNet -and -not $Rql) { throw "Pass -McpPlugin, -ReflectorNet and/or -Rql." }

$RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$targets = @('src', 'tests', 'testbed') | ForEach-Object {
    $p = Join-Path $RepoRoot $_
    if (Test-Path $p) { Get-ChildItem -Path $p -Recurse -Filter *.csproj }
}

$pins = @{}
if ($McpPlugin)    { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin']  = $McpPlugin }
if ($ReflectorNet) { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet'] = $ReflectorNet }
if ($Rql)          { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.Rql']          = $Rql }

foreach ($csproj in $targets) {
    $content = Get-Content $csproj.FullName -Raw
    $new = $content
    foreach ($id in $pins.Keys) {
        $pattern = '(<PackageReference\s+Include="' + [regex]::Escape($id) + '"\s+Version=")[^"]+(")'
        $new = [regex]::Replace($new, $pattern, "`${1}$($pins[$id])`${2}")
    }
    if ($new -ne $content) {
        Write-Host "Updating $($csproj.FullName.Substring($RepoRoot.Length+1))"
        foreach ($id in $pins.Keys) { Write-Host "  $id -> $($pins[$id])" }
        if (-not $WhatIf) { Set-Content -Path $csproj.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline }
    }
}
if ($WhatIf) { Write-Host "(WhatIf — no changes written)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
else { Write-Host "Done. Rebuild + test to confirm compatibility." -ForegroundColor Green }

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/commands/update-core.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Update the core MCP / reflection / query pins in lockstep across package/tests/testbed. Mirror of update-core.ps1.

The pins (com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin, com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet, com.IvanMurzak.Rql = the RQL module API) must
EQUAL the core Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP/Godot-MCP.csproj); scripts/extensions.py core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise.

Usage:
  python commands/update-core.py --mcp-plugin 6.11.0
  python commands/update-core.py --mcp-plugin 6.11.0 --reflector-net 5.4.0 --what-if
  python commands/update-core.py --rql 0.2.0
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--mcp-plugin")
    ap.add_argument("--reflector-net")
    ap.add_argument("--rql")
    ap.add_argument("--what-if", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not args.mcp_plugin and not args.reflector_net and not args.rql:
        raise SystemExit("error: pass --mcp-plugin, --reflector-net and/or --rql")

    pins = {}
    if args.mcp_plugin:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin"] = args.mcp_plugin
    if args.reflector_net:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet"] = args.reflector_net
    if args.rql:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.Rql"] = args.rql

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    csprojs = []
    for sub in ("src", "tests", "testbed"):
        d = root / sub
        if d.is_dir():
            csprojs += list(d.rglob("*.csproj"))

    for csproj in csprojs:
        content = csproj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        new = content
        for pid, ver in pins.items():
            new = re.sub(
                r'(<PackageReference\s+Include="' + re.escape(pid) + r'"\s+Version=")[^"]+(")',
                r"\g<1>" + ver + r"\g<2>", new)
        if new != content:
            print(f"Updating {csproj.relative_to(root)}")
            for pid, ver in pins.items():
                print(f"  {pid} -> {ver}")
            if not args.what_if:
                csproj.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="")

    print("(what-if — no changes written)" if args.what_if else "Done. Rebuild + test to confirm.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Animation/docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`:

```md
# The source-only NuGet recipe (the centerpiece)

A Godot-MCP extension is distributed as a **source-only** NuGet package: it ships C# **source**, not a
compiled DLL. The source compiles **inside the consumer's Godot project**, against the **consumer's own
GodotSharp**. This is what lets one package work across Godot versions with no bundled engine and no
version lock.

This recipe is **verified** end-to-end with `dotnet` alone (no Godot binary): build the package → unit
test → `dotnet pack` → restore+build a consumer `Godot.NET.Sdk` project that references it → the injected
source compiles clean against the consumer's GodotSharp.

## Why not a normal (DLL) package?

The RQL module calls Godot's C# API (`Node`, `Resource`, `EditorInterface`, …) which lives in
**GodotSharp**. A pre-compiled DLL is built against **one** GodotSharp version and is therefore locked to
it — a consumer on a different Godot version gets binary-incompatibility. Shipping **source** sidesteps
this: the consumer is itself a `Godot.NET.Sdk` project, so its build supplies GodotSharp at compile time
and our source compiles against *that* exact version.

## The three levers (in the package csproj)

```xml
<Project Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.3.0">   <!-- min-version floor; consumer uses its own -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>            <!-- (1) ship no DLL -->
    <DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>true</DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>  <!-- (3) -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU5128;NU1504</NoWarn>
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Only the MCP / reflection / query stack is a package dependency (the consumer already has it); pins = the core's. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin"   Version="8.14.0-dev.e8985d5" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql"         Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (3) GodotSharp is needed to COMPILE locally but must NOT be a package dependency. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp"            Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor"      Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'" />
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (2) Pack the .cs as plain files under src/ + the injection props under build/. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="Editor/**/*.cs"  Pack="true" PackagePath="src/Editor/" />
    <None Include="build/<PackageId>.props" Pack="true" PackagePath="build/" />
    <None Include="README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

**Lever 1 — no DLL.** `IncludeBuildOutput=false` keeps the compiled assembly out of the package; the
package's payload is the `.cs` files + the injection props.

**Lever 2 — inject source as `<Compile>` in the consumer.** The `.cs` are packed as plain files under
`src/`. The package ships `build/<PackageId>.props`, which **NuGet auto-imports** into any consuming
project (this is why the file MUST be named exactly `<PackageId>.props`). The props adds the packed `.cs`
as `<Compile>` items:

```xml
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\src\**\*.cs"
             Exclude="@(Compile)"
             Link="<PackageId>\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)` resolves into the NuGet cache (`…/<package>/<version>/build/`), so
`..\src\**\*.cs` is the packed source. The consumer's own default glob never reaches the cache, so
`Exclude="@(Compile)"` is just belt-and-suspenders against double-inclusion.

**Lever 3 — declare NO GodotSharp dependency.** The authoring project uses `Godot.NET.Sdk` so the
`Godot` namespace resolves and `#if TOOLS` compiles locally — but GodotSharp must NOT leak into the
package's dependency list (the consumer provides its own). Two steps are required because a plain
`<PackageReference Update="GodotSharp" PrivateAssets="all">` in the project body **does not work** (the
SDK adds GodotSharp *after* the body is evaluated, so there is nothing to update yet):

1. `DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences=true` drops the SDK's implicit `GodotSharp` + `GodotSharpEditor`.
2. Re-add `GodotSharp`/`GodotSharpEditor` explicitly with `PrivateAssets="all"` (kept for the local
   compile, excluded from the package deps). `Godot.SourceGenerators` has **no** SDK opt-out, so it is
   re-stated as an explicit `Include … PrivateAssets="all"` (this duplicates the implicit add → the
   harmless `NU1504`, suppressed via `NoWarn`).

Verify it worked by inspecting the generated `.nuspec` — its `<dependencies>` must list **only**
`com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`, with **no** `GodotSharp` /
`Godot.SourceGenerators`. CI asserts exactly this (`scripts/extensions.py` `verify_package`).

## Why `build/*.props` injection, not `contentFiles`?

NuGet's `contentFiles` with `buildAction="Compile"` is the other documented way to inject source. We use
the **`build/*.props`** mechanism instead because:

- **SDK-agnostic and deterministic.** It is plain MSBuild `<Compile Include>` — it does not depend on
  NuGet's `contentFiles`-Compile auto-injection behaving identically under `Godot.NET.Sdk` (which
  customizes globbing); the props is auto-imported the same way for every SDK.
- **One obvious file to read and override.** The whole injection is one short, visible props file rather
  than `contentFiles` metadata split between the nuspec and NuGet's restore-generated targets.
- **No double-compile risk.** `EnableDefaultNoneItems=false` + the explicit `<None Pack>` list controls
  exactly what ships; the consumer's project-dir glob never overlaps the cache.

`contentFiles` remains a valid alternative; if you switch, drop the props and pack the `.cs` under
`contentFiles/cs/any/…` with `buildAction="Compile"`, and re-verify the consumer build + the `.nuspec`
dependency list.

## Editor-only API: `#if TOOLS`

The RQL module, its adapters and sources sit behind `#if TOOLS`: RQL is the editor's data layer, so they
compile in the editor and are excluded from shipped games — exactly as in the core addon (Godot defines
`TOOLS` for the editor/Debug build and **not** for an exported game build). The agent guide and other
pure-managed helpers (validation rules, label maps) stay outside the guard so they are CI-unit-testable.
The core runs every RQL query on the editor main thread, so module code may touch `Node` / `Resource` /
`EditorInterface` directly.

## The consumer story

1. The consumer is a Godot **C#** project with the core `godot_mcp` addon enabled (which already
   references `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`).
2. Installing the extension adds one line to the consumer's `.csproj`:
   `<PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>" Version="x.y.z" />`
   (done by the **Extensions dock**, `godot-cli install-extension`, or by hand).
3. Rebuild. NuGet imports `build/<PackageId>.props` → the extension's `.cs` compile into the consumer's
   single project assembly against the consumer's GodotSharp.
4. The core's RQL engine discovers the module (`IRqlModule`) in the project assembly — **no registry edit**.
   Its adapters, sources and guide appear in `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` and the `godot-rql`
   skill, inside the user's real Godot editor.

## Publishing & the shared catalog

`release.yml` publishes the source-only package to NuGet (version-gated) and cuts an atomic GitHub
Release. To make the extension appear in the in-editor **Extensions** dock and `godot-cli
install-extension`, append one entry to the shared catalog `addons/godot_mcp/extensions.catalog.json` in
**Godot-MCP** (schema in `extensions.catalog.md`): `name`, `description`, `packageId`
(`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>`), optional `version`, `gitUrl`, and `tools` (empty for an RQL module). That
single source of truth is consumed by the dock, the CLI, and the app.

```
