`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/commands/init.ps1`:

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Initialize a new Godot-MCP extension from this template: replace placeholders, rename files/folders,
    and activate the CI workflows.

.DESCRIPTION
    From a single -Feature name (PascalCase, e.g. "Particles") this derives and substitutes every
    placeholder, then renames any file/folder whose name contains YOUR_FEATURE, then activates CI by
    renaming `.github/workflows/*.yml-sample` -> `*.yml`.

    Derived values (override any with the matching parameter):
      Package id  : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>     (the NuGet <PackageId>)
      Repo        : IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-<Feature>          (-GitHubRepository)
      Display name: "<Feature> Tools"                       (-DisplayName)
      Description : "RQL module for Godot <Feature>."      (-Description)
      RQL source  : <feature-lowercased>                     (-SourceName; the module's RQL source name)

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/init.ps1 -Feature "Particles"

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/init.ps1 -Feature "Particles" -GitHubRepository "myuser/Godot-AI-Particles" -DisplayName "Particle Tools"
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)] [string]$Feature,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$DisplayName,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$Description,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$GitHubRepository,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)][string]$SourceName
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

if ($Feature -notmatch '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$') {
    throw "Feature must be alphanumeric PascalCase (letters/digits, starts with a letter). Got: '$Feature'"
}

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($DisplayName))      { $DisplayName = "$Feature Tools" }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Description))       { $Description = "RQL module for Godot $Feature." }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($GitHubRepository))  { $GitHubRepository = "IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-$Feature" }
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($SourceName))        { $SourceName = $Feature.ToLower() }

$ScriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$RepoRoot  = Split-Path -Parent $ScriptDir

# Longest tokens first so no token is a prefix of another mid-replacement.
$Replacements = [ordered]@{
    "YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME_REPOSITORY" = $GitHubRepository
    "YOUR_DISPLAY_NAME"               = $DisplayName
    "YOUR_DESCRIPTION"                = $Description
    "YOUR_SOURCE"                     = $SourceName
    "YOUR_FEATURE"                    = $Feature
}

Write-Host "Initializing Godot-MCP extension:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "  Feature      : $Feature"
Write-Host "  Package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.$Feature"
Write-Host "  Repository   : $GitHubRepository"
Write-Host "  Display name : $DisplayName"
Write-Host "  RQL source   : $SourceName"
Write-Host ""

$ExcludeDirs = @('.git', 'bin', 'obj', '.godot', 'local-nuget', '.vs')

function Test-Excluded([string]$path) {
    foreach ($d in $ExcludeDirs) {
        if ($path -match "[\\/]$([regex]::Escape($d))([\\/]|$)") { return $true }
    }
    return $false
}

# 1) Replace placeholder content in all text files.
Write-Host "Replacing placeholders in file content..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$textExt = @('.cs','.csproj','.props','.targets','.md','.json','.yml','.yaml','.yml-sample','.godot','.config','.sh','.ps1','.py','.editorconfig','.gitignore','.txt')
Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoRoot -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object {
    $file = $_
    if (Test-Excluded $file.FullName) { return }
    if ($file.Name -eq 'init.ps1' -or $file.Name -eq 'init.py') { return }  # don't rewrite the running script
    $ext = $file.Extension.ToLower()
    $isText = ($textExt -contains $ext) -or ($file.Name -like '*.yml-sample') -or ($file.Name -eq 'LICENSE')
    if (-not $isText) { return }
    $content = Get-Content -Path $file.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($null -eq $content) { return }
    $new = $content
    foreach ($k in $Replacements.Keys) { $new = $new.Replace($k, $Replacements[$k]) }
    if ($new -ne $content) {
        Set-Content -Path $file.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline
        Write-Host "  updated $($file.FullName.Substring($RepoRoot.Length+1))" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    }
}

# 2) Rename files/folders whose NAME contains YOUR_FEATURE (deepest-first so children rename before parents).
Write-Host "Renaming files and folders..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path $RepoRoot -Recurse | Where-Object { -not (Test-Excluded $_.FullName) } |
    Sort-Object { $_.FullName.Length } -Descending | ForEach-Object {
        if ($_.Name -like '*YOUR_FEATURE*') {
            $newName = $_.Name.Replace('YOUR_FEATURE', $Feature)
            Rename-Item -Path $_.FullName -NewName $newName
            Write-Host "  renamed $($_.Name) -> $newName" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        }
    }

# 3) Activate CI: *.yml-sample -> *.yml
Write-Host "Activating CI workflows (*.yml-sample -> *.yml)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$wf = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".github/workflows"
if (Test-Path $wf) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $wf -Filter "*.yml-sample" | ForEach-Object {
        $target = $_.FullName -replace '\.yml-sample$', '.yml'
        Move-Item -Path $_.FullName -Destination $target -Force
        Write-Host "  activated $($_.Name) -> $([System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($target))" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Done. Next:" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  1. Review the changes, then build + test:"
Write-Host "       dotnet build src/Godot-AI-$Feature/Godot-AI-$Feature.csproj"
Write-Host "       dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-$Feature.Tests/Godot-AI-$Feature.Tests.csproj"
Write-Host "  2. Write the RQL module under src/Godot-AI-$Feature/Editor/Rql (adapters, sources, guide; see AGENTS.md)."
Write-Host "  3. Configure the NUGET_API_KEY secret, then push to main with a bumped <Version> to release."

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/commands/init.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Initialize a new Godot-MCP extension from this template (POSIX/Python path; mirrors init.ps1).

From a single --feature name (PascalCase, e.g. "Particles") this substitutes every placeholder, renames
files/folders whose name contains YOUR_FEATURE, then activates CI (*.yml-sample -> *.yml).

Derived (override with the matching flag):
  package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>
  repo         : IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-<Feature>      (--github-repository)
  display name : "<Feature> Tools"                   (--display-name)
  description  : "RQL module for Godot <Feature>."  (--description)
  RQL source   : <feature lowercased>                 (--source-name; the module's source, e.g. "particles | select …")

Usage:
  python commands/init.py --feature Particles
  python commands/init.py --feature Particles --github-repository myuser/Godot-AI-Particles
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXCLUDE_DIRS = {".git", "bin", "obj", ".godot", "local-nuget", ".vs"}
TEXT_EXT = {".cs", ".csproj", ".props", ".targets", ".md", ".json", ".yml", ".yaml",
            ".yml-sample", ".godot", ".config", ".sh", ".ps1", ".py", ".editorconfig",
            ".gitignore", ".txt"}
SELF = {"init.py", "init.ps1"}


def is_excluded(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
    rel_parts = path.relative_to(root).parts
    return any(part in EXCLUDE_DIRS for part in rel_parts)


def is_text(path: Path) -> bool:
    name = path.name
    if name == "LICENSE":
        return True
    if name.endswith(".yml-sample"):
        return True
    return path.suffix.lower() in TEXT_EXT


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Initialize a Godot-MCP extension from the template.")
    ap.add_argument("--feature", required=True, help="PascalCase feature name, e.g. Particles")
    ap.add_argument("--display-name")
    ap.add_argument("--description")
    ap.add_argument("--github-repository")
    ap.add_argument("--source-name")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    feature = args.feature
    if not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$", feature):
        print(f"error: --feature must be alphanumeric PascalCase. Got: {feature!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    display = args.display_name or f"{feature} Tools"
    description = args.description or f"RQL module for Godot {feature}."
    repo = args.github_repository or f"IvanMurzak/Godot-AI-{feature}"
    source = args.source_name or feature.lower()

    # Longest tokens first so no token is a prefix of another mid-replacement.
    replacements = [
        ("YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME_REPOSITORY", repo),
        ("YOUR_DISPLAY_NAME", display),
        ("YOUR_DESCRIPTION", description),
        ("YOUR_SOURCE", source),
        ("YOUR_FEATURE", feature),
    ]

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

    print("Initializing Godot-MCP extension:")
    print(f"  Feature      : {feature}")
    print(f"  Package id   : com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.{feature}")
    print(f"  Repository   : {repo}")
    print(f"  Display name : {display}")
    print(f"  RQL source   : {source}\n")

    # 1) Replace placeholder content.
    print("Replacing placeholders in file content...")
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file() or is_excluded(path, root) or path.name in SELF or not is_text(path):
            continue
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        new = text
        for token, value in replacements:
            new = new.replace(token, value)
        if new != text:
            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="")
            print(f"  updated {path.relative_to(root)}")

    # 2) Rename files/folders containing YOUR_FEATURE, deepest-first.
    print("Renaming files and folders...")
    entries = [p for p in root.rglob("*") if not is_excluded(p, root)]
    for path in sorted(entries, key=lambda p: len(str(p)), reverse=True):
        if "YOUR_FEATURE" in path.name:
            new_name = path.name.replace("YOUR_FEATURE", feature)
            path.rename(path.with_name(new_name))
            print(f"  renamed {path.name} -> {new_name}")

    # 3) Activate CI.
    print("Activating CI workflows (*.yml-sample -> *.yml)...")
    wf = root / ".github" / "workflows"
    if wf.is_dir():
        for sample in wf.glob("*.yml-sample"):
            target = sample.with_name(sample.name[: -len("-sample")])
            sample.replace(target)
            print(f"  activated {sample.name} -> {target.name}")

    print("\nDone. Next:")
    print(f"  dotnet build src/Godot-AI-{feature}/Godot-AI-{feature}.csproj")
    print(f"  dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-{feature}.Tests/Godot-AI-{feature}.Tests.csproj")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/commands/update-core.ps1`:

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Update the core MCP / reflection / query pins (com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin / com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet /
    com.IvanMurzak.Rql) in lockstep across the package, tests, and testbed csproj files.

.DESCRIPTION
    These pins MUST equal the core Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP/Godot-MCP.csproj; scripts/extensions.py
    core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise); com.IvanMurzak.Rql is the RQL module API. When the core advances its pins,
    run this in the same change. Pass any of the three.

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -McpPlugin "6.11.0"
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -McpPlugin "6.11.0" -ReflectorNet "5.4.0" -WhatIf
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/update-core.ps1 -Rql "0.2.0"
#>
param(
    [string]$McpPlugin,
    [string]$ReflectorNet,
    [string]$Rql,
    [switch]$WhatIf
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
if (-not $McpPlugin -and -not $ReflectorNet -and -not $Rql) { throw "Pass -McpPlugin, -ReflectorNet and/or -Rql." }

$RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$targets = @('src', 'tests', 'testbed') | ForEach-Object {
    $p = Join-Path $RepoRoot $_
    if (Test-Path $p) { Get-ChildItem -Path $p -Recurse -Filter *.csproj }
}

$pins = @{}
if ($McpPlugin)    { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin']  = $McpPlugin }
if ($ReflectorNet) { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet'] = $ReflectorNet }
if ($Rql)          { $pins['com.IvanMurzak.Rql']          = $Rql }

foreach ($csproj in $targets) {
    $content = Get-Content $csproj.FullName -Raw
    $new = $content
    foreach ($id in $pins.Keys) {
        $pattern = '(<PackageReference\s+Include="' + [regex]::Escape($id) + '"\s+Version=")[^"]+(")'
        $new = [regex]::Replace($new, $pattern, "`${1}$($pins[$id])`${2}")
    }
    if ($new -ne $content) {
        Write-Host "Updating $($csproj.FullName.Substring($RepoRoot.Length+1))"
        foreach ($id in $pins.Keys) { Write-Host "  $id -> $($pins[$id])" }
        if (-not $WhatIf) { Set-Content -Path $csproj.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline }
    }
}
if ($WhatIf) { Write-Host "(WhatIf — no changes written)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
else { Write-Host "Done. Rebuild + test to confirm compatibility." -ForegroundColor Green }

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/commands/update-core.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Update the core MCP / reflection / query pins in lockstep across package/tests/testbed. Mirror of update-core.ps1.

The pins (com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin, com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet, com.IvanMurzak.Rql = the RQL module API) must
EQUAL the core Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP/Godot-MCP.csproj); scripts/extensions.py core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise.

Usage:
  python commands/update-core.py --mcp-plugin 6.11.0
  python commands/update-core.py --mcp-plugin 6.11.0 --reflector-net 5.4.0 --what-if
  python commands/update-core.py --rql 0.2.0
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--mcp-plugin")
    ap.add_argument("--reflector-net")
    ap.add_argument("--rql")
    ap.add_argument("--what-if", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not args.mcp_plugin and not args.reflector_net and not args.rql:
        raise SystemExit("error: pass --mcp-plugin, --reflector-net and/or --rql")

    pins = {}
    if args.mcp_plugin:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin"] = args.mcp_plugin
    if args.reflector_net:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet"] = args.reflector_net
    if args.rql:
        pins["com.IvanMurzak.Rql"] = args.rql

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    csprojs = []
    for sub in ("src", "tests", "testbed"):
        d = root / sub
        if d.is_dir():
            csprojs += list(d.rglob("*.csproj"))

    for csproj in csprojs:
        content = csproj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        new = content
        for pid, ver in pins.items():
            new = re.sub(
                r'(<PackageReference\s+Include="' + re.escape(pid) + r'"\s+Version=")[^"]+(")',
                r"\g<1>" + ver + r"\g<2>", new)
        if new != content:
            print(f"Updating {csproj.relative_to(root)}")
            for pid, ver in pins.items():
                print(f"  {pid} -> {ver}")
            if not args.what_if:
                csproj.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="")

    print("(what-if — no changes written)" if args.what_if else "Done. Rebuild + test to confirm.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`:

```md
# The source-only NuGet recipe (the centerpiece)

A Godot-MCP extension is distributed as a **source-only** NuGet package: it ships C# **source**, not a
compiled DLL. The source compiles **inside the consumer's Godot project**, against the **consumer's own
GodotSharp**. This is what lets one package work across Godot versions with no bundled engine and no
version lock.

This recipe is **verified** end-to-end with `dotnet` alone (no Godot binary): build the package → unit
test → `dotnet pack` → restore+build a consumer `Godot.NET.Sdk` project that references it → the injected
source compiles clean against the consumer's GodotSharp.

## Why not a normal (DLL) package?

The RQL module calls Godot's C# API (`Node`, `Resource`, `EditorInterface`, …) which lives in
**GodotSharp**. A pre-compiled DLL is built against **one** GodotSharp version and is therefore locked to
it — a consumer on a different Godot version gets binary-incompatibility. Shipping **source** sidesteps
this: the consumer is itself a `Godot.NET.Sdk` project, so its build supplies GodotSharp at compile time
and our source compiles against *that* exact version.

## The three levers (in the package csproj)

```xml
<Project Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.3.0">   <!-- min-version floor; consumer uses its own -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>            <!-- (1) ship no DLL -->
    <DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>true</DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>  <!-- (3) -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU5128;NU1504</NoWarn>
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Only the MCP / reflection / query stack is a package dependency (the consumer already has it); pins = the core's. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin"   Version="8.14.0-dev.e8985d5" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql"         Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (3) GodotSharp is needed to COMPILE locally but must NOT be a package dependency. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp"            Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor"      Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'" />
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (2) Pack the .cs as plain files under src/ + the injection props under build/. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="Editor/**/*.cs"  Pack="true" PackagePath="src/Editor/" />
    <None Include="build/<PackageId>.props" Pack="true" PackagePath="build/" />
    <None Include="README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

**Lever 1 — no DLL.** `IncludeBuildOutput=false` keeps the compiled assembly out of the package; the
package's payload is the `.cs` files + the injection props.

**Lever 2 — inject source as `<Compile>` in the consumer.** The `.cs` are packed as plain files under
`src/`. The package ships `build/<PackageId>.props`, which **NuGet auto-imports** into any consuming
project (this is why the file MUST be named exactly `<PackageId>.props`). The props adds the packed `.cs`
as `<Compile>` items:

```xml
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\src\**\*.cs"
             Exclude="@(Compile)"
             Link="<PackageId>\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)` resolves into the NuGet cache (`…/<package>/<version>/build/`), so
`..\src\**\*.cs` is the packed source. The consumer's own default glob never reaches the cache, so
`Exclude="@(Compile)"` is just belt-and-suspenders against double-inclusion.

**Lever 3 — declare NO GodotSharp dependency.** The authoring project uses `Godot.NET.Sdk` so the
`Godot` namespace resolves and `#if TOOLS` compiles locally — but GodotSharp must NOT leak into the
package's dependency list (the consumer provides its own). Two steps are required because a plain
`<PackageReference Update="GodotSharp" PrivateAssets="all">` in the project body **does not work** (the
SDK adds GodotSharp *after* the body is evaluated, so there is nothing to update yet):

1. `DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences=true` drops the SDK's implicit `GodotSharp` + `GodotSharpEditor`.
2. Re-add `GodotSharp`/`GodotSharpEditor` explicitly with `PrivateAssets="all"` (kept for the local
   compile, excluded from the package deps). `Godot.SourceGenerators` has **no** SDK opt-out, so it is
   re-stated as an explicit `Include … PrivateAssets="all"` (this duplicates the implicit add → the
   harmless `NU1504`, suppressed via `NoWarn`).

Verify it worked by inspecting the generated `.nuspec` — its `<dependencies>` must list **only**
`com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`, with **no** `GodotSharp` /
`Godot.SourceGenerators`. CI asserts exactly this (`scripts/extensions.py` `verify_package`).

## Why `build/*.props` injection, not `contentFiles`?

NuGet's `contentFiles` with `buildAction="Compile"` is the other documented way to inject source. We use
the **`build/*.props`** mechanism instead because:

- **SDK-agnostic and deterministic.** It is plain MSBuild `<Compile Include>` — it does not depend on
  NuGet's `contentFiles`-Compile auto-injection behaving identically under `Godot.NET.Sdk` (which
  customizes globbing); the props is auto-imported the same way for every SDK.
- **One obvious file to read and override.** The whole injection is one short, visible props file rather
  than `contentFiles` metadata split between the nuspec and NuGet's restore-generated targets.
- **No double-compile risk.** `EnableDefaultNoneItems=false` + the explicit `<None Pack>` list controls
  exactly what ships; the consumer's project-dir glob never overlaps the cache.

`contentFiles` remains a valid alternative; if you switch, drop the props and pack the `.cs` under
`contentFiles/cs/any/…` with `buildAction="Compile"`, and re-verify the consumer build + the `.nuspec`
dependency list.

## Editor-only API: `#if TOOLS`

The RQL module, its adapters and sources sit behind `#if TOOLS`: RQL is the editor's data layer, so they
compile in the editor and are excluded from shipped games — exactly as in the core addon (Godot defines
`TOOLS` for the editor/Debug build and **not** for an exported game build). The agent guide and other
pure-managed helpers (validation rules, label maps) stay outside the guard so they are CI-unit-testable.
The core runs every RQL query on the editor main thread, so module code may touch `Node` / `Resource` /
`EditorInterface` directly.

## The consumer story

1. The consumer is a Godot **C#** project with the core `godot_mcp` addon enabled (which already
   references `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`).
2. Installing the extension adds one line to the consumer's `.csproj`:
   `<PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>" Version="x.y.z" />`
   (done by the **Extensions dock**, `godot-cli install-extension`, or by hand).
3. Rebuild. NuGet imports `build/<PackageId>.props` → the extension's `.cs` compile into the consumer's
   single project assembly against the consumer's GodotSharp.
4. The core's RQL engine discovers the module (`IRqlModule`) in the project assembly — **no registry edit**.
   Its adapters, sources and guide appear in `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` and the `godot-rql`
   skill, inside the user's real Godot editor.

## Publishing & the shared catalog

`release.yml` publishes the source-only package to NuGet (version-gated) and cuts an atomic GitHub
Release. To make the extension appear in the in-editor **Extensions** dock and `godot-cli
install-extension`, append one entry to the shared catalog `addons/godot_mcp/extensions.catalog.json` in
**Godot-MCP** (schema in `extensions.catalog.md`): `name`, `description`, `packageId`
(`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>`), optional `version`, `gitUrl`, and `tools` (empty for an RQL module). That
single source of truth is consumed by the dock, the CLI, and the app.

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/Editor/Rql/DialogicApi.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Godot;
using Rql;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The <c>dialogic</c> source: whether the addon is installed, the project's Dialogic files as read-only rows
    /// (<c>dialogic.timelines</c>, <c>dialogic.characters</c>) and the calls that create them. Dialogic works on resource
    /// files (<c>.dtl</c> timelines, <c>.dch</c> characters), not scene nodes. A character row holds the loaded resource in
    /// <c>resource</c>: <c>get resource | set props["…"]</c> writes it and the core saves the file (Dialogic's own saver).
    /// A timeline is its text, so lines are appended with the row's <c>AddText</c>. Creating and appending write files
    /// directly: they are not undoable (like <c>editor | call CreateResource</c>). Without the addon the lists are empty,
    /// <c>hint</c> says how to install it and the calls fail with that hint.
    /// </summary>
    [RqlDescription("Dialogic: installed, hint, timelines, characters; calls CreateTimeline, CreateCharacter")]
    public sealed class DialogicApi
    {
        // The source creates one instance per query: the class table and one walk of the editor filesystem (both file
        // kinds) are read once and shared by installed / hint / timelines / characters and the calls.
        private DialogicScripts? _scripts;
        private Dictionary<string, List<string>>? _files;

        internal DialogicScripts Scripts => _scripts ??= new DialogicScripts();

        [RqlDescription("whether the Dialogic addon is installed (its DialogicTimeline class is registered)")]
        public bool installed => Scripts.Has(DialogicNames.TimelineClass);

        [RqlDescription("how to install the addon when it is missing, else null")]
        public string? hint => installed ? null : DialogicNames.InstallHint;

        [RqlDescription("every .dtl timeline of the project (res://addons skipped): path name eventCount text resource; call AddText")]
        public List<DialogicTimelineRow> timelines => Rows(DialogicNames.TimelineExtension, path => new DialogicTimelineRow(path, this));

        [RqlDescription("every .dch character of the project (res://addons skipped): path name displayName color description resource")]
        public List<DialogicCharacterRow> characters => Rows(DialogicNames.CharacterExtension, path => new DialogicCharacterRow(path));

        [RqlCallable("create a timeline file (res://….dtl; .dtl is appended when missing) with one text line (speaker optional; no text: a two-line starter); fails if the file exists; not undoable; returns its path")]
        public string CreateTimeline(string path, string? text = null, string? speaker = null)
        {
            RequireInstalled();
            var resPath = NewFilePath(path, DialogicNames.TimelineExtension, "timelines");
            SaveTimeline(resPath, string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(text) ? DialogicNames.StarterTimelineText() : DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(speaker, text));
            return resPath;
        }

        [RqlCallable("create a character file (res://….dch; .dch is appended when missing) with a display name, a color (\"#rrggbb\", default \"#3aa0ff\") and a description; fails if the file exists; not undoable; returns its path")]
        public string CreateCharacter(string path, string displayName, string? color = null, string? description = null)
        {
            RequireInstalled();
            Check(DialogicRules.DisplayName(displayName));
            Check(DialogicRules.Color(color, out var hex));
            var resPath = NewFilePath(path, DialogicNames.CharacterExtension, "characters");
            var character = Scripts.New(DialogicNames.CharacterClass);
            character.Set(DialogicNames.DisplayName, displayName.Trim());
            character.Set(DialogicNames.Color, global::Godot.Color.FromHtml(hex));
            character.Set(DialogicNames.Description, description ?? string.Empty);
            Save(character, resPath);
            return resPath;
        }

        /// <summary>Write a timeline's text to its file through Dialogic's saver and make the saved resource the cached one.</summary>
        internal void SaveTimeline(string resPath, string text)
        {
            var timeline = Scripts.New(DialogicNames.TimelineClass);
            timeline.Call(DialogicNames.FromTextMethod, text);
            timeline.SetMeta(DialogicNames.NotSavedMeta, true);
            Save(timeline, resPath);
        }

        internal void RequireInstalled()
        {
            if (!installed) throw new InvalidOperationException(DialogicNames.InstallHint);
        }

        private List<T> Rows<T>(string extension, Func<string, T> make)
        {
            var list = new List<T>();
            if (installed)
                foreach (var path in Files(extension)) list.Add(make(path));
            return list;
        }

        private static void Save(Resource resource, string resPath)
        {
            var dir = resPath.Substring(0, resPath.LastIndexOf('/'));
            if (dir != "res:/" && !DirAccess.DirExistsAbsolute(dir))
            {
                var made = DirAccess.MakeDirRecursiveAbsolute(dir);
                if (made != Error.Ok) throw new InvalidOperationException($"could not create the folder '{dir}': {made}");
            }
            var error = ResourceSaver.Save(resource, resPath);
            if (error != Error.Ok) throw new InvalidOperationException($"could not save '{resPath}': {error}");
            resource.TakeOverPath(resPath);
            EditorInterface.Singleton.GetResourceFilesystem()?.UpdateFile(resPath);
        }

        private static string NewFilePath(string path, string extension, string list)
        {
            Check(DialogicRules.ResourcePath(path, extension, out var resPath));
            if (FileAccess.FileExists(resPath)) throw new ArgumentException($"'{resPath}' already exists (read it from dialogic.{list})");
            return resPath;
        }

        private static void Check(string? reason)
        {
            if (reason != null) throw new ArgumentException(reason);
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// The res:// files with the extension, sorted, from the editor filesystem index (one walk for both extensions per
        /// query; res://addons skipped).
        /// </summary>
        private List<string> Files(string extension)
        {
            if (_files == null)
            {
                _files = new Dictionary<string, List<string>>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
                {
                    [DialogicNames.TimelineExtension] = new List<string>(),
                    [DialogicNames.CharacterExtension] = new List<string>(),
                };
                if (EditorInterface.Singleton.GetResourceFilesystem()?.GetFilesystem() is { } root) Collect(root, _files, isRoot: true);
                foreach (var found in _files.Values) found.Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal);
            }
            return _files[extension];
        }

        private static void Collect(EditorFileSystemDirectory dir, Dictionary<string, List<string>> files, bool isRoot)
        {
            var fileCount = dir.GetFileCount();
            for (int i = 0; i < fileCount; i++)
            {
                var path = dir.GetFilePath(i);
                var dot = path.LastIndexOf('.');
                if (dot >= 0 && files.TryGetValue(path.Substring(dot + 1), out var list)) list.Add(path);
            }
            var subCount = dir.GetSubdirCount();
            for (int i = 0; i < subCount; i++)
                if (dir.GetSubdir(i) is { } sub && !(isRoot && sub.GetName() == "addons")) Collect(sub, files, isRoot: false);
        }
    }
}
#endif

```

/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System;
using Godot;
using Rql;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One Dialogic character file (a row of <c>dialogic.characters</c>), read live from the loaded resource. Read-only;
    /// change a character through <c>resource</c> (<c>get resource | set props["display_name"] = "Hero"</c>): the core
    /// writes the property and saves the .dch file with Dialogic's saver.
    /// </summary>
    [RqlDescription("Dialogic character (read-only row): path name displayName color description resource; write through resource")]
    public sealed class DialogicCharacterRow
    {
        private readonly Lazy<Resource?> _resource;

        internal DialogicCharacterRow(string path)
        {
            this.path = path;
            _resource = new Lazy<Resource?>(() => ResourceLoader.Load(path));
        }

        [RqlDescription("res:// path of the .dch file")]
        public string path { get; }

        [RqlDisplay, RqlDescription("file name without the extension (the name a timeline's \"Name: text\" line uses)")]
        public string name => path.Substring(path.LastIndexOf('/') + 1).GetBaseName();

        [RqlDescription("display name (props[\"display_name\"])")]
        public string? displayName => resource?.Get(DialogicNames.DisplayName).AsString();

        [RqlDescription("name color as \"#rrggbb\" (props[\"color\"])")]
        public string? color => resource == null ? null : "#" + resource.Get(DialogicNames.Color).AsColor().ToHtml(false).ToLowerInvariant();

        [RqlDescription("description (props[\"description\"])")]
        public string? description => resource?.Get(DialogicNames.Description).AsString();

        [RqlReference, RqlDescription("the DialogicCharacter resource: write through it (get resource | set props[\"description\"] = \"…\"), the .dch is saved")]
        public Resource? resource => _resource.Value;
    }
}
#endif

    /// <summary>
    /// The Dialogic addon's names, the contract of the module: its resource classes are GDScript <c>class_name</c>s (no C#
    /// type, not in ClassDB), so they are referenced by string only. Verified against <c>dialogic-godot/dialogic</c>
    /// 2.0-alpha-18 / -20. Pure-managed (no Godot API), so it is unit-tested.
    /// </summary>
    public static class DialogicNames
    {
        public const string TimelineClass = "DialogicTimeline";
        public const string CharacterClass = "DialogicCharacter";

        public const string TimelineExtension = "dtl";
        public const string CharacterExtension = "dch";

        // DialogicCharacter's GDScript properties (snake_case, read / written with props["…"]).
        public const string DisplayName = "display_name";
        public const string Color = "color";
        public const string Description = "description";

        // DialogicTimeline: from_text(text) parses the .dtl text; its saver writes only when this meta is set.
        public const string FromTextMethod = "from_text";
        public const string NotSavedMeta = "timeline_not_saved";

        public const string InstallHint =
            "Dialogic is not installed: install 'Dialogic' (Godot Asset Library, or dialogic-godot/dialogic 2.0 into " +
            "res://addons/dialogic/), enable it under Project Settings -> Plugins so its Dialogic autoload is registered, " +
            "then rebuild.";

        /// <summary>The first lines of a timeline created without text.</summary>
        public static string StarterTimelineText() =>
            DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("Narrator", "Welcome to your new Dialogic timeline!") + "\n" +
            DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(null, "Edit it in the Dialogic editor, or append lines with AddText.");

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/Editor/Rql/DialogicRules.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using System;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The checks of the module's creation calls, run before anything is written. Each returns the rejection reason, or
    /// null when the value is valid (normalized values come back through out parameters). Pure-managed (no Godot API), so
    /// it is unit-tested.
    /// </summary>
    public static class DialogicRules
    {
        /// <summary>The default character color (a friendly blue), as six hex digits.</summary>
        public const string DefaultColor = "3aa0ff";

        /// <summary>
        /// A res:// file path for a Dialogic resource: backslashes become slashes, a missing <c>res://</c> is added and a
        /// missing extension is appended (<c>res://intro</c> → <c>res://intro.dtl</c>); another extension is rejected, and
        /// so is a <c>..</c> segment (res:// is not sandboxed: it would write, and create folders, outside the project).
        /// </summary>
        public static string? ResourcePath(string? path, string extension, out string normalized)
        {
            normalized = string.Empty;
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(path)) return $"a res:// path for the .{extension} file is required";
            var p = path!.Trim().Replace('\\', '/');
            if (p.StartsWith("user://", StringComparison.Ordinal) || p.Contains("://") && !p.StartsWith("res://", StringComparison.Ordinal))
                return $"'{path}' is not a res:// path";
            if (!p.StartsWith("res://", StringComparison.Ordinal)) p = "res://" + p.TrimStart('/');
            if (Array.IndexOf(p.Substring("res://".Length).Split('/'), "..") >= 0)
                return $"'{path}' must not contain a '..' segment (it would leave the project folder)";
            var file = p.Substring(p.LastIndexOf('/') + 1);
            if (file.Length == 0) return $"'{path}' names a folder, not a .{extension} file";
            var dot = file.LastIndexOf('.');
            if (dot < 0) p += "." + extension;
            else if (!string.Equals(file.Substring(dot + 1), extension, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
                return $"'{path}' must be a .{extension} file";
            normalized = p;
            return null;
        }

        /// <summary>A character needs a display name.</summary>
        public static string? DisplayName(string? displayName) =>
            string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(displayName) ? "a character needs a display name" : null;

        /// <summary>
        /// A color as <c>#rrggbb</c> (or <c>rrggbb</c>, <c>#rrggbbaa</c>, any case); empty means <see cref="DefaultColor"/>.
        /// <paramref name="hex"/> receives the six lower-case digits.
        /// </summary>
        public static string? Color(string? value, out string hex)
        {
            hex = DefaultColor;
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value)) return null;
            var s = value!.Trim();
            if (s.StartsWith("#", StringComparison.Ordinal)) s = s.Substring(1);
            s = s.ToLowerInvariant();
            if ((s.Length == 6 || s.Length == 8) && IsHex(s))
            {
                hex = s.Substring(0, 6);
                return null;
            }
            return $"color must be a hex color like \"#e91e63\" (got '{value}')";
        }

        private static bool IsHex(string s)
        {
            foreach (var c in s)
                if (!((c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f'))) return false;
            return true;
        }
    }
}

/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Godot;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The project's GDScript global classes (<c>class_name</c> to script path), read from
    /// <c>ProjectSettings.GetGlobalClassList()</c> once per source access (the source creates one per query). A GDScript
    /// node or resource reports its native base from <c>GetClass()</c>, so its Dialogic class comes from its script chain
    /// (<see cref="Chain"/>). The Beehave, Dialogic and PhantomCamera extensions each carry this same class: a shared source
    /// would define the type twice in a consumer that installs two of them.
    /// </summary>
    internal sealed class DialogicScripts
    {
        private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _pathByClass = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);

        public DialogicScripts()
        {
            foreach (global::Godot.Collections.Dictionary entry in ProjectSettings.GetGlobalClassList())
                if (entry.TryGetValue("class", out var name) && entry.TryGetValue("path", out var path))
                    _pathByClass[name.AsString()] = path.AsString();
        }

        /// <summary>True when the global class is registered (the addon is installed and its scripts parsed).</summary>
        public bool Has(string className) => _pathByClass.ContainsKey(className);

        /// <summary>The script path of a global class, or null.</summary>
        public string? PathOf(string className) => _pathByClass.TryGetValue(className, out var path) ? path : null;

        /// <summary>
        /// The global class names of the object's script and its base scripts, nearest first; null when it has none
        /// (a plain node allocates nothing).
        /// </summary>
        public static List<string>? Chain(GodotObject o)
        {
            List<string>? chain = null;
            for (var script = o.GetScript().As<Script>(); script != null; script = script.GetBaseScript())
            {
                var name = script.GetGlobalName().ToString();
                if (name.Length > 0) (chain ??= new List<string>()).Add(name);
            }
            return chain;
        }

        /// <summary>A new instance of a global resource class (Dialogic resources have no C# type and are not in ClassDB).</summary>
        public Resource New(string className)
        {
            var path = PathOf(className);
            var script = path != null && ResourceLoader.Exists(path) ? GD.Load<GDScript>(path) : null;
            return script?.New().As<Resource>()
                ?? throw new InvalidOperationException($"could not create a {className}: {DialogicNames.InstallHint}");
        }
    }
}
#endif

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/Editor/Rql/DialogicTimelineRow.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using Godot;
using Rql;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One Dialogic timeline file (a row of <c>dialogic.timelines</c>). A timeline is its text (one event per line), read
    /// from the file; append a text line with <c>AddText</c> (writes the file, not undoable).
    /// </summary>
    [RqlDescription("Dialogic timeline (read-only row): path name eventCount text resource; call AddText(text, speaker?)")]
    public sealed class DialogicTimelineRow
    {
        private readonly DialogicApi _api;
        private string? _text;

        internal DialogicTimelineRow(string path, DialogicApi api)
        {
            this.path = path;
            _api = api;
        }

        [RqlDescription("res:// path of the .dtl file")]
        public string path { get; }

        [RqlDisplay, RqlDescription("file name without the extension (Dialogic's timeline identifier)")]
        public string name => path.Substring(path.LastIndexOf('/') + 1).GetBaseName();

        [RqlDescription("the timeline text (Dialogic's .dtl format: one event per line, \"Speaker: text\" for a text event)")]
        public string text => _text ??= FileAccess.GetFileAsString(path);

        [RqlDescription("number of non-empty lines (events) in the text")]
        public int eventCount => DialogicTimelineText.CountEvents(text);

        [RqlReference, RqlDescription("the DialogicTimeline resource (loaded on access)")]
        public Resource? resource => ResourceLoader.Load(path);

        [RqlCallable("append a text event (\"Speaker: text\"; speaker optional, colons escaped) to the timeline file; not undoable; returns the new event count")]
        public int AddText(string text, string? speaker = null)
        {
            _api.RequireInstalled();
            var combined = DialogicTimelineText.Append(FileAccess.GetFileAsString(path), DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(speaker, text));
            _api.SaveTimeline(path, combined);
            _text = combined;
            return DialogicTimelineText.CountEvents(combined);
        }
    }
}
#endif

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/Editor/Rql/DialogicTimelineText.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Pure-managed (CI-unit-testable) helper for Dialogic's <b>plain-text timeline format</b> — the
    /// version-stable surface the module writes. A Dialogic <c>.dtl</c> file IS its timeline text (the
    /// addon's loader does <c>from_text(file.get_as_text())</c>), so building one line of text is the whole job
    /// and it can be verified with no Godot binary.
    ///
    /// <para>
    /// A text event is a single line: <c>text</c> for narration, or <c>Speaker: text</c> when a character
    /// speaks (mirrors Dialogic 2.0-alpha-19's <c>DialogicTextEvent.to_text()</c>: colons in the body are
    /// escaped as <c>\:</c> and a speaker name containing spaces is wrapped in quotes).
    /// </para>
    /// </summary>
    public static class DialogicTimelineText
    {
        /// <summary>Placeholder body Dialogic uses for an empty text event.</summary>
        public const string EmptyEventBody = "<Empty Text Event>";

        /// <summary>
        /// Build one text-event line. The body's colons are escaped (<c>:</c> → <c>\:</c>); a non-empty
        /// <paramref name="speaker"/> is prefixed as <c>Speaker: </c> (quoted when it contains spaces). An
        /// empty body becomes <see cref="EmptyEventBody"/>.
        /// </summary>
        public static string BuildTextLine(string? speaker, string? text)
        {
            var body = (text ?? string.Empty).Replace(":", "\\:").Trim();
            if (body.Length == 0)
                body = EmptyEventBody;

            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(speaker))
                return body;

            var name = speaker!.Trim();
            if (name.Contains(" "))
                name = "\"" + name + "\"";

            return name + ": " + body;
        }

        /// <summary>
        /// Append <paramref name="newLine"/> as a new line to <paramref name="existingText"/> (trimming a
        /// trailing newline first). When the existing text is empty, returns <paramref name="newLine"/> alone.
        /// </summary>
        public static string Append(string? existingText, string newLine)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(existingText))
                return newLine;
            return existingText!.TrimEnd('\n', '\r') + "\n" + newLine;
        }

        /// <summary>Count the non-empty lines (≈ text events) in a timeline's text.</summary>
        public static int CountEvents(string? text)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(text)) return 0;
            var lines = text!.Replace("\r\n", "\n").Split('\n');
            var count = 0;
            foreach (var line in lines)
                if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line))
                    count++;
            return count;
        }
    }
}

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/Godot-AI-Dialogic.csproj`:

```csproj
<!--
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SOURCE-ONLY NuGet package recipe — the load-bearing detail of a Godot-MCP extension.          │
  │  Full rationale + the consumer story: docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md.                        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Why source-only? An extension's RQL module (adapters, sources, methods) calls Godot's C# API (Node,
  Resource, EditorInterface, …). Shipping a
  pre-compiled DLL would LOCK the package to one GodotSharp version. Instead we ship the .cs SOURCE and
  let it compile INSIDE the consumer's Godot project, against the CONSUMER's own GodotSharp (supplied by
  their `Godot.NET.Sdk`). No bundled Godot, no version lock.

  How (3 levers):
    1. <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>  — do NOT put this project's compiled DLL in the package.
    2. The .cs are packed under `src/` (plain files) and injected as <Compile> items in the consumer by
       `build/<PackageId>.props` (auto-imported by NuGet). See that props file.
    3. NO GodotSharp dependency is declared (DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences + PrivateAssets=all below)
       — the consumer provides it. Only the MCP / reflection / query stack is declared as a (min-version) dependency,
       which the consumer already has via the core Godot-MCP addon.

  This project ALSO uses `Godot.NET.Sdk` for AUTHORING only: so the editor-only module (#if TOOLS) compiles
  + the `Godot` namespace resolves when you build/test locally.
  No Godot binary is needed — `Godot.NET.Sdk` pulls `GodotSharp` from NuGet at compile time.
-->
<Project Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.3.0">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <RootNamespace>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic</AssemblyName>

    <!-- ===== Package identity (bump-version.ps1 / get-version.ps1 own the Version element) ===== -->
    <IsPackable>true</IsPackable>
    <PackageId>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic</PackageId>
    <Version>1.0.1</Version>
    <Title>Dialogic Tools</Title>
    <Authors>Ivan Murzak</Authors>
    <Description>RQL module for Godot Dialogic.</Description>
    <PackageTags>godot;mcp;ai;tools;godot-mcp;ai-game-developer</PackageTags>
    <PackageLicenseExpression>Apache-2.0</PackageLicenseExpression>
    <PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
    <RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP</RepositoryUrl>
    <PackageProjectUrl>https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP</PackageProjectUrl>
    <RepositoryType>git</RepositoryType>

    <!-- ===== Source-only levers ===== -->
    <!-- 1) Do not ship the compiled DLL; the consumer compiles our source against their GodotSharp. -->
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
    <!-- NU5128: source-only package (dependencies but no lib/ref) — expected, silence it.
         NU1504: Godot.SourceGenerators is re-stated PrivateAssets=all to keep it out of deps (see below). -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU5128;NU1504</NoWarn>
    <NoPackageAnalysis>true</NoPackageAnalysis>
    <!-- We hand-pick exactly which files ship (below); turn off default None globbing to avoid duplicates. -->
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
    <!-- Drop the SDK's implicit GodotSharp/GodotSharpEditor so we can re-add them PrivateAssets=all (a body
         <PackageReference Update> does NOT work — the SDK adds them after the project body is evaluated). -->
    <DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>true</DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    Package DEPENDENCIES: only the engine-agnostic MCP / reflection / query stack (com.IvanMurzak.Rql is the RQL
    module API: IRqlModule, type adapters). A NuGet Version="x" is a ">= x" floor; the pins EQUAL the core
    Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP.csproj; scripts/extensions.py core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise): a lower
    ReflectorNet than the McpPlugin requires is a NU1605 downgrade, a higher pin cannot restore in a consumer
    pinned to the core. `update-core.ps1` / `update-core.py` keep package, tests and testbed in lockstep.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin" Version="8.14.0-dev.e8985d5" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql" Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    GodotSharp is needed for AUTHORING compile only, NOT as a package dependency (the consumer supplies its
    own, version-matched). PrivateAssets=all stops these flowing into the package's dependency list — this
    is the "no GodotSharp dependency" guarantee, verified by inspecting the generated .nuspec.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'" />
    <!-- Godot.SourceGenerators has no SDK opt-out property, so re-state it (Include) PrivateAssets=all to
         keep it out of the package deps too. This duplicates the SDK's implicit add -> NU1504 (suppressed
         above). The analyzer still runs locally (PrivateAssets governs only what flows to CONSUMERS). -->
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    What ships in the .nupkg:
      • the .cs SOURCE under `src/` (plain files — NOT contentFiles; injected by the props below),
      • `build/<PackageId>.props` (auto-imported by NuGet in the consumer; does the <Compile> injection),
      • README.md (package page).
    The .cs are <Compile> items in THIS authoring build (Godot.NET.Sdk default glob) so they compile +
    unit-test locally; adding them to <None Pack="true"> just also bundles them into the package.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="Editor/**/*.cs" Pack="true" PackagePath="src/Editor/" />
    <None Include="build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.props" Pack="true" PackagePath="build/" />
    <None Include="README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/README.md`:

```md
# Dialogic Tools

RQL module for the Godot Dialogic addon: a dialogic source that lists timelines and characters, creates them and appends timeline text.

Optional Godot-MCP extension, independently versioned as NuGet package `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic` (1.0.1).
Requires a Godot C# project (4.4.0+) with a core `godot_mcp` addon that has the RQL tools
(`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, the release after 0.28.0).

## Required prerequisite — Dialogic (install it yourself)

This extension **does NOT include** the Dialogic addon and does not download or vendor it. You must
install Dialogic into your own Godot project separately:

- Install **Dialogic** from the **Godot Asset Library**, or from
  **https://github.com/dialogic-godot/dialogic** (tested against **2.0-alpha-18 on Godot 4.4** and **2.0-alpha-20 on Godot 4.5+**).
- Enable it under **Project Settings → Plugins** (this also registers the `Dialogic` autoload).

Without Dialogic installed and enabled, `dialogic | select installed hint` reports `false` with an install hint,
the `dialogic` lists are empty and its calls fail with that hint (by design).

> Dialogic is © Emilio Coppola and contributors, distributed under the **MIT License**. This extension is
> **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by** the Dialogic project — it merely provides an RQL module
> that authors its resources. See the addon's own repository for its licence and terms.

## Install

```sh
godot-cli install-plugin /path/to/project
godot-cli install-extension com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic /path/to/project
godot-cli build /path/to/project
```

The installer resolves the latest stable version from NuGet; use `--version 1.0.1` to request an exact version.
Packages contain C# source and build props, compiled against the project's own GodotSharp.
Previous NuGet versions remain installable after the repository migration.

## RQL

Since 1.0.0 the extension is an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools. Agents create and read Dialogic timelines and
characters with the core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools, and the module's guide is part of the core
`godot-rql` skill. Dialogic stores dialogue in resource files whose classes are GDScript `class_name`s (the core
`editor | call CreateResource` cannot make them), so the module adds:

- **The `dialogic` source**: `installed`, `hint` (how to install the addon when it is missing), the project's files as
  **read-only rows** (`dialogic.timelines`: `path name eventCount text resource`; `dialogic.characters`: `path name
  displayName color description resource`; `res://addons` and hidden folders are skipped), and the calls
  `CreateTimeline(path, text?, speaker?)` and `CreateCharacter(path, displayName, color?, description?)` (validated:
  `.dtl` / `.dch` paths, an existing file, a hex color, a display name).
- **`AddText(text, speaker?)`** on a timeline row appends a text line (a timeline is its text).
- **Character writes go through the row's `resource`** (`get resource | set props["…"]`): the core writes the
  property and saves the `.dch` with Dialogic's own saver.

Creating and appending write the files directly and are **not undoable** (like `CreateResource`).

```
dialogic | select installed hint
dialogic | call CreateTimeline("res://e2e_intro.dtl", "Hello from CI", "Narrator")
dialogic | call CreateCharacter("res://e2e_hero.dch", "Hero", "#e91e63", "The brave protagonist.")
dialogic.timelines | where name == "e2e_intro" | call AddText("A second line", "Hero")
dialogic.characters | where name == "e2e_hero" | get resource | set props["description"] = "The bravest hero."
dialogic.timelines | select path eventCount text
dialogic.characters | select path displayName color description
```

Without the addon the module still loads: `dialogic | select installed hint` returns `false` and the install hint,
the lists are empty and the calls fail with the hint.

### Migrating from 0.x

| 0.x tool | RQL |
| --- | --- |
| `dialogic-defaults` | removed: `CreateTimeline(path)` without text writes the two-line starter; the guide lists typical values ("Narrator", color "#3aa0ff") |
| `dialogic-timeline-create` | `rql-mutate` `dialogic \| call CreateTimeline("res://intro.dtl", "Hello", "Narrator")` (now fails if the file exists) |
| `dialogic-character-create` | `rql-mutate` `dialogic \| call CreateCharacter("res://hero.dch", "Hero", "#e91e63", "…")` (an invalid color now fails instead of falling back) |
| `dialogic-timeline-add-text` | `rql-mutate` `dialogic.timelines \| where name == "intro" \| call AddText("A second line", "Hero")` |
| `dialogic-get` | `rql-query` `dialogic.timelines \| select path eventCount text` / `dialogic.characters \| select path displayName color description` |
| `Installed: false` results | `dialogic \| select installed hint` |

## Development and releases

See the [monorepo test and release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md).
This module retains its own package, version, tests and Apache-2.0 [license](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/LICENSE).
Releasing another module does not rebuild or republish this package.

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/src/Godot-AI-Dialogic/build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.props`:

```props
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SOURCE INJECTION — the consumer half of the source-only package recipe.                       │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  NuGet auto-imports `build/<PackageId>.props` into any project that references this package. This file
  MUST be named exactly `<PackageId>.props` (com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.props) or NuGet will
  not import it. `bump-version` / `init` keep the name in lockstep with <PackageId>.

  It adds this package's packed `.cs` (which sit in the NuGet cache under `<package>/<version>/src/`) as
  <Compile> items in the CONSUMER's project, so they compile INSIDE the consumer's Godot project against
  the consumer's own GodotSharp. Because the consumer is a `Godot.NET.Sdk` project, `Godot` types resolve
  and `#if TOOLS` is defined for the editor build — exactly as if the source lived in the consumer's repo.

  • $(MSBuildThisFileDirectory) resolves to `<package>/<version>/build/` in the NuGet cache, so
    `../src/**/*.cs` is the packed source.
  • Exclude="@(Compile)" is belt-and-suspenders against double-inclusion (the consumer's own default
    glob never reaches the NuGet cache, so it normally excludes nothing).
  • Link groups the injected files under the package id in IDEs (cosmetic).
-->
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\src\**\*.cs"
             Exclude="@(Compile)"
             Link="com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using System.Linq;
using Rql.Execution;
using Xunit;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.Tests
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The module configures cleanly (without the addon and without Godot) and shapes its view types: the <c>dialogic</c>
    /// source with its creation calls, its guide, and read-only rows. Metadata only: no member that touches Godot is read.
    /// </summary>
    public class DialogicModuleTests
    {
        private static RqlEngine Engine()
        {
            var engine = new RqlEngine();
            var reports = engine.AddModulesFrom(new[] { typeof(DialogicModule).Assembly });
            Assert.All(reports, r => Assert.True(r.Ok, r.ToString()));
            Assert.Contains(reports, r => r.Module == typeof(DialogicModule).FullName);
            return engine;
        }

        [Fact]
        public void ModuleRegistersItsSourceAndGuide()
        {
            var engine = Engine();
            Assert.True(engine.Sources.ContainsKey("dialogic"));
            var guide = Assert.Single(engine.Guides, g => g.Key == DialogicGuide.Topic);
            Assert.Equal(DialogicGuide.Markdown, guide.Value);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TheSourceHasItsListsAndCreationCalls()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(DialogicApi));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "installed", "hint", "timelines", "characters" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
            var timeline = Assert.Single(info.Callable, c => c.Name == "CreateTimeline");
            Assert.Equal(new[] { false, true, true }, timeline.Parameters.Select(p => p.HasDefault));
            var character = Assert.Single(info.Callable, c => c.Name == "CreateCharacter");
            Assert.Equal(new[] { false, false, true, true }, character.Parameters.Select(p => p.HasDefault));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TimelineRowsAreReadOnlyWithAddText()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(DialogicTimelineRow));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "path", "name", "text", "eventCount", "resource" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
            var addText = Assert.Single(info.Callable, c => c.Name == "AddText");
            Assert.Equal(new[] { false, true }, addText.Parameters.Select(p => p.HasDefault));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void CharacterRowsAreReadOnlyAndHoldTheResource()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(DialogicCharacterRow));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "path", "name", "displayName", "color", "description", "resource" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
            Assert.Empty(info.Callable);
        }
    }
}

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/tests/Godot-AI-Dialogic.Tests/DialogicRulesTests.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using Xunit;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.Tests
{
    public class DialogicRulesTests
    {
        [Theory]
        [InlineData("res://e2e_intro.dtl", "res://e2e_intro.dtl")]
        [InlineData("res://e2e_intro", "res://e2e_intro.dtl")]
        [InlineData("dialogue/intro", "res://dialogue/intro.dtl")]
        [InlineData("/dialogue/intro.DTL", "res://dialogue/intro.DTL")]
        [InlineData("dialogue\\intro.dtl", "res://dialogue/intro.dtl")]
        public void TimelinePathsAreNormalized(string path, string expected)
        {
            Assert.Null(DialogicRules.ResourcePath(path, "dtl", out var normalized));
            Assert.Equal(expected, normalized);
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(null, "is required")]
        [InlineData("  ", "is required")]
        [InlineData("res://hero.dtl", "must be a .dch file")]
        [InlineData("res://characters/", "names a folder")]
        [InlineData("user://hero.dch", "not a res:// path")]
        [InlineData("res://../outside/hero.dch", "'..' segment")]
        [InlineData("characters/../../hero", "'..' segment")]
        public void BadCharacterPathsAreRejected(string? path, string reason) =>
            Assert.Contains(reason, DialogicRules.ResourcePath(path, "dch", out _));

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(null, "3aa0ff")]
        [InlineData("", "3aa0ff")]
        [InlineData("#E91E63", "e91e63")]
        [InlineData("e91e63", "e91e63")]
        [InlineData("#e91e63ff", "e91e63")]
        public void ColorsAreHexOrTheDefault(string? value, string hex)
        {
            Assert.Null(DialogicRules.Color(value, out var normalized));
            Assert.Equal(hex, normalized);
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData("red")]
        [InlineData("#zzz")]
        [InlineData("#12345")]
        public void OtherColorsAreRejected(string value) =>
            Assert.StartsWith("color must be a hex color", DialogicRules.Color(value, out _));

        [Fact]
        public void ACharacterNeedsADisplayName()
        {
            Assert.Null(DialogicRules.DisplayName("Hero"));
            Assert.NotNull(DialogicRules.DisplayName(" "));
            Assert.NotNull(DialogicRules.DisplayName(null));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TheStarterTimelineHasTwoLines()
        {
            Assert.Equal(2, DialogicTimelineText.CountEvents(DialogicNames.StarterTimelineText()));
            Assert.StartsWith("Narrator: ", DialogicNames.StarterTimelineText());
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TheInstallHintNamesTheAddonAndItsAutoload()
        {
            Assert.Contains("dialogic-godot/dialogic", DialogicNames.InstallHint);
            Assert.Contains("Dialogic autoload", DialogicNames.InstallHint);
        }
    }
}

`extensions/Godot-AI-Dialogic/tests/Godot-AI-Dialogic.Tests/DialogicTimelineTextTests.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using Xunit;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.Tests
{
    /// <summary>Unit spec for the pure-managed Dialogic plain-text timeline-format helper.</summary>
    public class DialogicTimelineTextTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void BuildTextLine_PlainText_NoSpeaker()
        {
            Assert.Equal("Hello world", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(null, "Hello world"));
            Assert.Equal("Hello world", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("  ", "Hello world"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BuildTextLine_WithSpeaker_PrependsName()
        {
            Assert.Equal("Hero: Hello world", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("Hero", "Hello world"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BuildTextLine_SpeakerWithSpaces_IsQuoted()
        {
            Assert.Equal("\"Dark Knight\": Hello", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("Dark Knight", "Hello"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BuildTextLine_EscapesColonsInBody()
        {
            // The body's colons are escaped (':' -> '\:'); the speaker separator colon is NOT escaped.
            Assert.Equal("Hero: Time\\: 10\\:00", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("Hero", "Time: 10:00"));
            Assert.Equal("Note\\: hi", DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(null, "Note: hi"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BuildTextLine_EmptyBody_UsesPlaceholder()
        {
            Assert.Equal(DialogicTimelineText.EmptyEventBody, DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine(null, ""));
            Assert.Equal("Hero: " + DialogicTimelineText.EmptyEventBody, DialogicTimelineText.BuildTextLine("Hero", "   "));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void Append_ToEmpty_ReturnsLineAlone()
        {
            Assert.Equal("line", DialogicTimelineText.Append(null, "line"));
            Assert.Equal("line", DialogicTimelineText.Append("", "line"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void Append_ToExisting_JoinsWithNewline()
        {
            Assert.Equal("a\nb", DialogicTimelineText.Append("a", "b"));
            Assert.Equal("a\nb", DialogicTimelineText.Append("a\n", "b"));
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(null, 0)]
        [InlineData("", 0)]
        [InlineData("one", 1)]
        [InlineData("one\ntwo", 2)]
        [InlineData("one\n\n  \ntwo\n", 2)]
        public void CountEvents_CountsNonEmptyLines(string? text, int expected)
        {
            Assert.Equal(expected, DialogicTimelineText.CountEvents(text));
        }
    }
}

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <!--
    Unit-test project for the Dialogic RQL module. A PLAIN xUnit assembly (Microsoft.NET.Sdk), NOT a Godot game
    project — so it builds + runs in CI with no Godot binary.

    It compiles the module sources directly (no ProjectReference to the Godot.NET.Sdk package project), with TOOLS
    defined so the #if TOOLS module and its views compile too. Only managed metadata is exercised: the RQL engine
    configures the module and builds the member tables of its view types by reflection; no Godot object is ever
    created (native-backed objects crash a plain test host). Live Dialogic nodes are verified by the headless-Godot
    E2E (tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json), which runs every guide example.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup>

    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
    <RootNamespace>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.Tests</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Dialogic.Tests</AssemblyName>
    <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);TOOLS</DefineConstants>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.11.1" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit" Version="2.9.2" />
    <PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.2" />
    <!-- The package's RQL pin (IRqlModule, adapters, the parser for the guide examples) and the Godot API it
         compiles against (metadata only here). -->
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql" Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp" Version="4.3.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor" Version="4.3.0" />

    <Compile Include="..\..\..\Shared\Tests\*.cs" Link="Shared\%(Filename)%(Extension)" />

`extensions/Godot-AI-GridMap/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# AGENTS.md — Godot-AI-GridMap

A **Godot-MCP extension** for Godot's built-in `GridMap` node (3D tile maps over a `MeshLibrary`), shipped as an
**RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools, only what the core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools need to
paint grids (validated settings, cell rows, `SetCell` / `ClearCell` / `Clear`, an agent guide rendered into the
core `godot-rql` skill). A **source-only NuGet package** (`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.GridMap`) compiled inside the
consumer's Godot project against the consumer's own GodotSharp; the packaging recipe is in
`docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`.

## Layout

- `src/Godot-AI-GridMap/Editor/Rql/` — the module:
  - `GridMapModule.cs` — the `IRqlModule` (Order 100, `#if TOOLS`): the adapter and the guide.
  - `Godot_GridMap_Adapter.cs` — `CellSize` / `CellOctantSize` (validated), `cells`, `cellCount`, the cell calls
    (`#if TOOLS`).
  - Pure-managed, NOT behind `#if TOOLS`: `GridMapRules.cs` (validation), `GridMapGuide.cs` (the guide),
    `GridMapCellRow.cs` (the read-only `cells` row).
- `src/Godot-AI-GridMap/build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.GridMap.props` — source-injection props, auto-imported by
  NuGet in the consumer; MUST stay named `<PackageId>.props`.
- `tests/Godot-AI-GridMap.Tests/` — xUnit (no Godot binary): rules, guide examples parse, the module's member
  table (GodotSharp metadata, `TOOLS` defined), and the e2e manifest runs every guide example.
- `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` — the live calls (`rql-*`), driven by `scripts/extension_e2e.py` from the monorepo suite.
- `testbed/` — consumer project restoring the local-packed package (injection proof) and `e2e-meshlib.tres`, the
  empty MeshLibrary fixture the e2e assigns (copied to the live project root).
- `commands/` — `bump-version`, `update-core`, `init` (`.ps1` + `.py`), `get-version.ps1`.
- CI and publishing are centralized in the monorepo; see `../../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md`.

## Critical invariants

- **RQL surface.** Everything is registered by `GridMapModule` and documented in `GridMapGuide` (topic
  "GridMap"). Every guide example runs, in order, in `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` (xUnit-asserted).
- **Validate, never clamp.** Members and calls reject what Godot refuses (cell size below 0.001, octant size 0,
  coordinates beyond ±32767, orientation outside 0..23) or 0.x refused (negative items: erase with `ClearCell`)
  before anything changes, so Godot never logs an error (the headless suite fails on any `ERROR:`).
- Never select or edit nodes (`EditorInterface.EditNode`): the 0.x tool's selection raised a native GridMap gizmo
  error in the headless editor. The calls are on the GridMap itself, so the core undo snapshot covers its cells.
- The namespace ends in `.GridMap`, which shadows `Godot.GridMap`: use the `GdGridMap` alias.
- The module uses only Godot, `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` and the BCL, never core-addon types (the authoring build has
  no core). Undo, dirty marking and saving come from the core's mutation hooks.

## Build / test (no Godot binary)

```bash
dotnet build src/Godot-AI-GridMap/Godot-AI-GridMap.csproj -c Debug   # the module (#if TOOLS included)
dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-GridMap.Tests/Godot-AI-GridMap.Tests.csproj
```

The live suite (one headless editor for every module) is `python scripts/test_extensions.py` from the monorepo
root. `dotnet pack` reuses the **global NuGet cache** for an already-cached version: when re-packing the same
`Version`, clear `~/.nuget/packages/com.ivanmurzak.godot.mcp.gridmap/<ver>` (or pack a unique version).

## Conventions

- Root namespace `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.GridMap`. Every `.cs` starts with the Apache-2.0 header and
  `#nullable enable`.
- The package declares only the `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin` / `ReflectorNet` / `Rql` pins (equal to the core's); **GodotSharp must
  never become a package dependency** (CI asserts the nuspec). Bump them with `commands/update-core.ps1`.

```
