`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`:

```md
# The source-only NuGet recipe (the centerpiece)

A Godot-MCP extension is distributed as a **source-only** NuGet package: it ships C# **source**, not a
compiled DLL. The source compiles **inside the consumer's Godot project**, against the **consumer's own
GodotSharp**. This is what lets one package work across Godot versions with no bundled engine and no
version lock.

This recipe is **verified** end-to-end with `dotnet` alone (no Godot binary): build the package → unit
test → `dotnet pack` → restore+build a consumer `Godot.NET.Sdk` project that references it → the injected
source compiles clean against the consumer's GodotSharp.

## Why not a normal (DLL) package?

The RQL module calls Godot's C# API (`Node`, `Resource`, `EditorInterface`, …) which lives in
**GodotSharp**. A pre-compiled DLL is built against **one** GodotSharp version and is therefore locked to
it — a consumer on a different Godot version gets binary-incompatibility. Shipping **source** sidesteps
this: the consumer is itself a `Godot.NET.Sdk` project, so its build supplies GodotSharp at compile time
and our source compiles against *that* exact version.

## The three levers (in the package csproj)

```xml
<Project Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.3.0">   <!-- min-version floor; consumer uses its own -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>            <!-- (1) ship no DLL -->
    <DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>true</DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>  <!-- (3) -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU5128;NU1504</NoWarn>
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Only the MCP / reflection / query stack is a package dependency (the consumer already has it); pins = the core's. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin"   Version="8.14.0-dev.e8985d5" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql"         Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (3) GodotSharp is needed to COMPILE locally but must NOT be a package dependency. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp"            Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor"      Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'" />
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- (2) Pack the .cs as plain files under src/ + the injection props under build/. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="Editor/**/*.cs"  Pack="true" PackagePath="src/Editor/" />
    <None Include="build/<PackageId>.props" Pack="true" PackagePath="build/" />
    <None Include="README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

**Lever 1 — no DLL.** `IncludeBuildOutput=false` keeps the compiled assembly out of the package; the
package's payload is the `.cs` files + the injection props.

**Lever 2 — inject source as `<Compile>` in the consumer.** The `.cs` are packed as plain files under
`src/`. The package ships `build/<PackageId>.props`, which **NuGet auto-imports** into any consuming
project (this is why the file MUST be named exactly `<PackageId>.props`). The props adds the packed `.cs`
as `<Compile>` items:

```xml
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\src\**\*.cs"
             Exclude="@(Compile)"
             Link="<PackageId>\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

`$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)` resolves into the NuGet cache (`…/<package>/<version>/build/`), so
`..\src\**\*.cs` is the packed source. The consumer's own default glob never reaches the cache, so
`Exclude="@(Compile)"` is just belt-and-suspenders against double-inclusion.

**Lever 3 — declare NO GodotSharp dependency.** The authoring project uses `Godot.NET.Sdk` so the
`Godot` namespace resolves and `#if TOOLS` compiles locally — but GodotSharp must NOT leak into the
package's dependency list (the consumer provides its own). Two steps are required because a plain
`<PackageReference Update="GodotSharp" PrivateAssets="all">` in the project body **does not work** (the
SDK adds GodotSharp *after* the body is evaluated, so there is nothing to update yet):

1. `DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences=true` drops the SDK's implicit `GodotSharp` + `GodotSharpEditor`.
2. Re-add `GodotSharp`/`GodotSharpEditor` explicitly with `PrivateAssets="all"` (kept for the local
   compile, excluded from the package deps). `Godot.SourceGenerators` has **no** SDK opt-out, so it is
   re-stated as an explicit `Include … PrivateAssets="all"` (this duplicates the implicit add → the
   harmless `NU1504`, suppressed via `NoWarn`).

Verify it worked by inspecting the generated `.nuspec` — its `<dependencies>` must list **only**
`com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`, with **no** `GodotSharp` /
`Godot.SourceGenerators`. CI asserts exactly this (`scripts/extensions.py` `verify_package`).

## Why `build/*.props` injection, not `contentFiles`?

NuGet's `contentFiles` with `buildAction="Compile"` is the other documented way to inject source. We use
the **`build/*.props`** mechanism instead because:

- **SDK-agnostic and deterministic.** It is plain MSBuild `<Compile Include>` — it does not depend on
  NuGet's `contentFiles`-Compile auto-injection behaving identically under `Godot.NET.Sdk` (which
  customizes globbing); the props is auto-imported the same way for every SDK.
- **One obvious file to read and override.** The whole injection is one short, visible props file rather
  than `contentFiles` metadata split between the nuspec and NuGet's restore-generated targets.
- **No double-compile risk.** `EnableDefaultNoneItems=false` + the explicit `<None Pack>` list controls
  exactly what ships; the consumer's project-dir glob never overlaps the cache.

`contentFiles` remains a valid alternative; if you switch, drop the props and pack the `.cs` under
`contentFiles/cs/any/…` with `buildAction="Compile"`, and re-verify the consumer build + the `.nuspec`
dependency list.

## Editor-only API: `#if TOOLS`

The RQL module, its adapters and sources sit behind `#if TOOLS`: RQL is the editor's data layer, so they
compile in the editor and are excluded from shipped games — exactly as in the core addon (Godot defines
`TOOLS` for the editor/Debug build and **not** for an exported game build). The agent guide and other
pure-managed helpers (validation rules, label maps) stay outside the guard so they are CI-unit-testable.
The core runs every RQL query on the editor main thread, so module code may touch `Node` / `Resource` /
`EditorInterface` directly.

## The consumer story

1. The consumer is a Godot **C#** project with the core `godot_mcp` addon enabled (which already
   references `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin`, `com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet` and `com.IvanMurzak.Rql`).
2. Installing the extension adds one line to the consumer's `.csproj`:
   `<PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>" Version="x.y.z" />`
   (done by the **Extensions dock**, `godot-cli install-extension`, or by hand).
3. Rebuild. NuGet imports `build/<PackageId>.props` → the extension's `.cs` compile into the consumer's
   single project assembly against the consumer's GodotSharp.
4. The core's RQL engine discovers the module (`IRqlModule`) in the project assembly — **no registry edit**.
   Its adapters, sources and guide appear in `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` and the `godot-rql`
   skill, inside the user's real Godot editor.

## Publishing & the shared catalog

`release.yml` publishes the source-only package to NuGet (version-gated) and cuts an atomic GitHub
Release. To make the extension appear in the in-editor **Extensions** dock and `godot-cli
install-extension`, append one entry to the shared catalog `addons/godot_mcp/extensions.catalog.json` in
**Godot-MCP** (schema in `extensions.catalog.md`): `name`, `description`, `packageId`
(`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.<Feature>`), optional `version`, `gitUrl`, and `tools` (empty for an RQL module). That
single source of truth is consumed by the dock, the CLI, and the app.

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Editor/Rql/PhantomCameraApi.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Godot;
using Rql;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The <c>phantomcamera</c> source: whether the addon is installed and its nodes in the edited scene as read-only rows
    /// (<c>phantomcamera.cameras</c>, <c>phantomcamera.hosts</c>). A row names the node's Phantom Camera class (a GDScript
    /// class_name the C# type cannot show), shows the modes by name and holds the node itself in <c>node</c>: writes go
    /// through it (<c>get node | set props["…"]</c>, undoable), plus the validated <c>SetFollow</c> / <c>SetLookAt</c>
    /// calls on a camera row. Without the addon the lists are empty and <c>hint</c> says how to install it.
    /// </summary>
    [RqlDescription("Phantom Camera: installed, hint, cameras, hosts")]
    public sealed class PhantomCameraApi
    {
        // The source creates one instance per query: the class table and one scene walk (cameras and hosts together) are
        // read once and shared by installed / hint / cameras / hosts.
        private PhantomCameraScripts? _scripts;
        private List<PhantomCameraRow>? _cameras;
        private List<PhantomCameraHostRow>? _hosts;

        private PhantomCameraScripts Scripts => _scripts ??= new PhantomCameraScripts();

        [RqlDescription("whether the Phantom Camera addon is installed (its PhantomCamera3D class is registered)")]
        public bool installed => Scripts.Has(PhantomCameraNames.PhantomCamera3D);

        [RqlDescription("how to install the addon when it is missing, else null")]
        public string? hint => installed ? null : PhantomCameraNames.InstallHint;

        [RqlDescription("every PhantomCamera3D / PhantomCamera2D of the edited scene, depth-first: name path scriptClass priority followMode followTarget lookAtMode lookAtTarget followDamping lookAtDamping node; calls SetFollow, SetLookAt")]
        public List<PhantomCameraRow> cameras
        {
            get { Walk(); return _cameras!; }
        }

        [RqlDescription("every PhantomCameraHost of the edited scene: name path camera (the Camera3D / Camera2D it drives) node")]
        public List<PhantomCameraHostRow> hosts
        {
            get { Walk(); return _hosts!; }
        }

        private void Walk()
        {
            if (_cameras != null) return;
            _cameras = new List<PhantomCameraRow>();
            _hosts = new List<PhantomCameraHostRow>();
            var root = EditorInterface.Singleton.GetEditedSceneRoot();
            if (root == null || !installed) return;
            var stack = new Stack<Node>();
            stack.Push(root);
            while (stack.Count > 0)
            {
                var node = stack.Pop();
                if (PhantomCameraScripts.Chain(node) is { } chain)
                {
                    var is3D = chain.Contains(PhantomCameraNames.PhantomCamera3D);
                    if (is3D || chain.Contains(PhantomCameraNames.PhantomCamera2D))
                        _cameras.Add(new PhantomCameraRow(node, root, chain[0], !is3D));
                    else if (chain.Contains(PhantomCameraNames.PhantomCameraHost))
                        _hosts.Add(new PhantomCameraHostRow(node, root, chain[0]));
                }
                var children = node.GetChildren();
                for (int i = children.Count - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.Push(children[i]);
            }
        }

        /// <summary>The path of a node below the edited scene root, or null when it is not in that scene.</summary>
        internal static string? PathInScene(Node root, Node? node)
        {
            if (node == null || !GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(node)) return null;
            return node == root || root.IsAncestorOf(node) ? root.GetPathTo(node).ToString() : null;
        }
    }
}
#endif

            "A scene needs one PhantomCameraHost under its Camera3D (Camera2D in 2D); the highest `priority` camera (at least 0, " +

            "damping on (props[\"follow_damping\"], props[\"look_at_damping\"]). Other settings are Godot properties of the " +
            "camera node (`props[\"follow_offset\"]`, `props[\"tween_resource\"]` …). " +
            "Without the addon `phantomcamera | select installed hint` says so and the lists are empty.";

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Editor/Rql/PhantomCameraModes.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using System;
using System.Globalization;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera
{
    /// <summary>PhantomCamera3D / PhantomCamera2D <c>FollowMode</c> (the 2D camera has no ThirdPerson).</summary>
    public enum PhantomFollowMode
    {
        None = 0,
        Glued = 1,
        Simple = 2,
        Group = 3,
        Path = 4,
        Framed = 5,
        ThirdPerson = 6
    }

    /// <summary>PhantomCamera3D <c>LookAtMode</c> (the 2D camera has none).</summary>
    public enum PhantomLookAtMode
    {
        None = 0,
        Mimic = 1,
        Simple = 2,
        Group = 3
    }

    /// <summary>Mode names to the addon's enum ints and back. Pure-managed, unit-tested.</summary>
    public static class PhantomCameraModes
    {
        /// <summary>The label of a mode int ("Simple", "ThirdPerson"; an unknown int as its number).</summary>
        public static string Label<T>(int value) where T : struct, Enum =>
            Enum.IsDefined(typeof(T), value) ? Enum.GetName(typeof(T), value)! : value.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

        /// <summary>
        /// A mode by name, case-insensitive, ignoring '_', '-' and spaces ("third_person", "Third Person" match ThirdPerson);
        /// numbers are not names and are rejected.
        /// </summary>
        public static bool TryParse<T>(string? value, out T mode) where T : struct, Enum
        {
            var name = (value ?? string.Empty).Trim().Replace("_", "").Replace("-", "").Replace(" ", "");
            mode = default;
            if (name.Length == 0 || char.IsDigit(name[0]) || name[0] == '+') return false;
            return Enum.TryParse(name, ignoreCase: true, out mode) && Enum.IsDefined(typeof(T), mode);
        }
    }
}

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Editor/Rql/PhantomCameraRow.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System;
using Godot;
using Rql;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera
{
    /// <summary>
    /// One PhantomCamera3D / PhantomCamera2D of the edited scene (a row of <c>phantomcamera.cameras</c>): its settings read
    /// live from the node, the modes by name. Read-only; plain settings change through <c>node</c>
    /// (<c>get node | set props["priority"] = 50</c>, undoable). <c>SetFollow</c> / <c>SetLookAt</c> set a mode by name and
    /// its target in the order the addon needs, validated by <see cref="PhantomCameraRules"/>; they are calls on this row,
    /// not on the node, so they are NOT undoable: they mark the scene unsaved themselves.
    /// </summary>
    [RqlDescription("PhantomCamera3D / 2D (read-only row): name path scriptClass priority followMode followTarget lookAtMode lookAtTarget followDamping lookAtDamping node; calls SetFollow(mode, target?), SetLookAt(mode, target?)")]
    public sealed class PhantomCameraRow
    {
        private readonly bool _is2D;
        private readonly Node _root;

        internal PhantomCameraRow(Node node, Node root, string scriptClass, bool is2D)
        {
            this.node = node;
            _root = root;
            path = root.GetPathTo(node).ToString();
            this.scriptClass = scriptClass;
            _is2D = is2D;
        }

        [RqlDisplay, RqlDescription("node name")]
        public string name => node.Name.ToString();

        [RqlDescription("path below the edited scene root")]
        public string path { get; }

        [RqlDescription("PhantomCamera3D or PhantomCamera2D (or your class_name extending one)")]
        public string scriptClass { get; }

        [RqlDescription("priority (props[\"priority\"]): the highest-priority camera drives the host's Camera3D / Camera2D; at least 0")]
        public int priority => node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.Priority).AsInt32();

        [RqlDescription("None, Glued, Simple, Group, Path, Framed or ThirdPerson (3D only); set it with SetFollow")]
        public string followMode => PhantomCameraModes.Label<PhantomFollowMode>(node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.FollowMode).AsInt32());

        [RqlDescription("path of the followed node (props[\"follow_target\"]), or null")]
        public string? followTarget => PhantomCameraApi.PathInScene(_root, node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.FollowTarget).As<Node>());

        [RqlDescription("None, Mimic, Simple or Group (null for a PhantomCamera2D); set it with SetLookAt")]
        public string? lookAtMode => _is2D ? null : PhantomCameraModes.Label<PhantomLookAtMode>(node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.LookAtMode).AsInt32());

        [RqlDescription("path of the looked-at node (props[\"look_at_target\"]), or null")]
        public string? lookAtTarget => _is2D ? null : PhantomCameraApi.PathInScene(_root, node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.LookAtTarget).As<Node>());

        [RqlDescription("whether following is damped (props[\"follow_damping\"])")]
        public bool followDamping => node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.FollowDamping).AsBool();

        [RqlDescription("whether looking at is damped (props[\"look_at_damping\"]; null for a PhantomCamera2D)")]
        public bool? lookAtDamping => _is2D ? null : node.Get(PhantomCameraNames.LookAtDamping).AsBool();

        [RqlReference, RqlDescription("the camera node: write plain settings through it (get node | set props[\"priority\"] = 50)")]
        public Node node { get; }

        [RqlCallable("set the follow mode by name (None, Glued, Simple, Group, Path, Framed, ThirdPerson) and, optionally, the node to follow (a Node3D / Node2D; set after the mode, which the addon requires); validated; NOT undoable, marks the scene unsaved; returns the follow mode")]
        public string SetFollow(string mode, Node? target = null)
        {
            Check(PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode(mode, _is2D, out var followMode));
            Apply(PhantomCameraNames.FollowMode, (int)followMode, PhantomCameraNames.FollowTarget, target, () => PhantomCameraRules.FollowTarget(followMode));
            return followMode.ToString();
        }

        [RqlCallable("set the look-at mode by name (None, Mimic, Simple, Group; PhantomCamera3D only) and, optionally, the Node3D to look at (set after the mode, which the addon requires); validated; NOT undoable, marks the scene unsaved; returns the look-at mode")]
        public string SetLookAt(string mode, Node? target = null)
        {
            Check(PhantomCameraRules.LookAtMode(mode, _is2D, out var lookAtMode));
            Apply(PhantomCameraNames.LookAtMode, (int)lookAtMode, PhantomCameraNames.LookAtTarget, target, () => PhantomCameraRules.LookAtTarget(lookAtMode));
            return lookAtMode.ToString();
        }

        // Validate the target first, then write the mode and the target in the order the addon requires. When the addon
        // refuses the target, the previous mode and target are restored so a failed call changes nothing.
        private void Apply(string modeProperty, int mode, string targetProperty, Node? target, Func<string?> targetRule)
        {
            if (target != null)
            {
                Check(targetRule());
                CheckTarget(target);
            }
            var previousMode = node.Get(modeProperty);
            var previousTarget = node.Get(targetProperty);
            node.Set(modeProperty, mode);
            if (target != null)
            {
                try { SetTarget(targetProperty, target); }
                catch
                {
                    node.Set(modeProperty, previousMode);
                    node.Set(targetProperty, previousTarget);
                    throw;
                }
            }
            EditorInterface.Singleton.MarkSceneAsUnsaved();
        }

        private void CheckTarget(Node target) =>
            Check(PhantomCameraRules.TargetType(_is2D, _is2D ? target is Node2D : target is Node3D, target.Name.ToString(), target.GetClass()));

        private void SetTarget(string property, Node target)
        {
            node.Set(property, target);
            if (node.Get(property).As<Node>() != target)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Phantom Camera did not accept '{target.Name}' as {property}");
        }

        private static void Check(string? reason)
        {
            if (reason != null) throw new ArgumentException(reason);
        }
    }
}
#endif

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Editor/Rql/PhantomCameraRules.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The checks of the camera rows' <c>SetFollow</c> / <c>SetLookAt</c>, run before anything is written. Each returns the
    /// rejection reason, or null when the value is valid. The addon's own setters ignore a target silently when the mode
    /// takes none (None, Group), which is why those combinations are rejected. Pure-managed (no Godot API), so it is
    /// unit-tested.
    /// </summary>
    public static class PhantomCameraRules
    {
        public static string? FollowMode(string? name, bool is2D, out PhantomFollowMode mode)
        {
            if (!PhantomCameraModes.TryParse(name, out mode))
                return $"unknown follow mode '{name}': use None, Glued, Simple, Group, Path, Framed{(is2D ? "" : " or ThirdPerson")}";
            if (is2D && mode == PhantomFollowMode.ThirdPerson)
                return "ThirdPerson is a PhantomCamera3D follow mode; a PhantomCamera2D has None, Glued, Simple, Group, Path, Framed";
            return null;
        }

        public static string? LookAtMode(string? name, bool is2D, out PhantomLookAtMode mode)
        {
            mode = PhantomLookAtMode.None;
            if (is2D) return "a PhantomCamera2D has no look-at mode (only a PhantomCamera3D does)";
            return PhantomCameraModes.TryParse(name, out mode)
                ? null
                : $"unknown look-at mode '{name}': use None, Mimic, Simple or Group";
        }

        /// <summary>A single follow target only applies to the modes that follow one node.</summary>
        public static string? FollowTarget(PhantomFollowMode mode) => mode switch
        {
            PhantomFollowMode.None => "follow mode None follows nothing: omit the target",
            PhantomFollowMode.Group => "follow mode Group follows the list props[\"follow_targets\"], not one target: omit the target and set that list",
            _ => null,
        };

        /// <summary>A single look-at target only applies to the modes that look at one node.</summary>
        public static string? LookAtTarget(PhantomLookAtMode mode) => mode switch
        {
            PhantomLookAtMode.None => "look-at mode None looks at nothing: omit the target",
            PhantomLookAtMode.Group => "look-at mode Group looks at the list props[\"look_at_targets\"], not one target: omit the target and set that list",
            _ => null,
        };

        /// <summary>A 3D camera follows / looks at a Node3D, a 2D camera a Node2D.</summary>
        public static string? TargetType(bool is2D, bool targetMatches, string targetName, string targetClass) =>
            targetMatches ? null : $"target '{targetName}' is a {targetClass}; a {(is2D ? "PhantomCamera2D needs a Node2D" : "PhantomCamera3D needs a Node3D")}";
    }
}

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Editor/Rql/PhantomCameraScripts.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#if TOOLS
#nullable enable
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Godot;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The project's GDScript global classes (<c>class_name</c> to script path), read from
    /// <c>ProjectSettings.GetGlobalClassList()</c> once per source access (the source creates one per query). A GDScript
    /// node or resource reports its native base from <c>GetClass()</c>, so its Phantom Camera class comes from its script chain
    /// (<see cref="Chain"/>). The Beehave, Dialogic and PhantomCamera extensions each carry this same class: a shared source
    /// would define the type twice in a consumer that installs two of them.
    /// </summary>
    internal sealed class PhantomCameraScripts
    {
        private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _pathByClass = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);

        public PhantomCameraScripts()
        {
            foreach (global::Godot.Collections.Dictionary entry in ProjectSettings.GetGlobalClassList())
                if (entry.TryGetValue("class", out var name) && entry.TryGetValue("path", out var path))
                    _pathByClass[name.AsString()] = path.AsString();
        }

        /// <summary>True when the global class is registered (the addon is installed and its scripts parsed).</summary>
        public bool Has(string className) => _pathByClass.ContainsKey(className);

        /// <summary>The script path of a global class, or null.</summary>
        public string? PathOf(string className) => _pathByClass.TryGetValue(className, out var path) ? path : null;

        /// <summary>
        /// The global class names of the object's script and its base scripts, nearest first; null when it has none
        /// (a plain node allocates nothing).
        /// </summary>
        public static List<string>? Chain(GodotObject o)
        {
            List<string>? chain = null;
            for (var script = o.GetScript().As<Script>(); script != null; script = script.GetBaseScript())
            {
                var name = script.GetGlobalName().ToString();
                if (name.Length > 0) (chain ??= new List<string>()).Add(name);
            }
            return chain;
        }
    }
}
#endif

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera.csproj`:

```csproj
<!--
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SOURCE-ONLY NuGet package recipe — the load-bearing detail of a Godot-MCP extension.          │
  │  Full rationale + the consumer story: docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md.                        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Why source-only? An extension's RQL module (adapters, sources, methods) calls Godot's C# API (Node,
  Resource, EditorInterface, …). Shipping a
  pre-compiled DLL would LOCK the package to one GodotSharp version. Instead we ship the .cs SOURCE and
  let it compile INSIDE the consumer's Godot project, against the CONSUMER's own GodotSharp (supplied by
  their `Godot.NET.Sdk`). No bundled Godot, no version lock.

  How (3 levers):
    1. <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>  — do NOT put this project's compiled DLL in the package.
    2. The .cs are packed under `src/` (plain files) and injected as <Compile> items in the consumer by
       `build/<PackageId>.props` (auto-imported by NuGet). See that props file.
    3. NO GodotSharp dependency is declared (DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences + PrivateAssets=all below)
       — the consumer provides it. Only the MCP / reflection / query stack is declared as a (min-version) dependency,
       which the consumer already has via the core Godot-MCP addon.

  This project ALSO uses `Godot.NET.Sdk` for AUTHORING only: so the editor-only module (#if TOOLS) compiles
  + the `Godot` namespace resolves when you build/test locally.
  No Godot binary is needed — `Godot.NET.Sdk` pulls `GodotSharp` from NuGet at compile time.
-->
<Project Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.3.0">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <RootNamespace>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera</AssemblyName>

    <!-- ===== Package identity (bump-version.ps1 / get-version.ps1 own the Version element) ===== -->
    <IsPackable>true</IsPackable>
    <PackageId>com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera</PackageId>
    <Version>1.0.1</Version>
    <Title>PhantomCamera Tools</Title>
    <Authors>Ivan Murzak</Authors>
    <Description>RQL module for Godot PhantomCamera.</Description>
    <PackageTags>godot;mcp;ai;tools;godot-mcp;ai-game-developer</PackageTags>
    <PackageLicenseExpression>Apache-2.0</PackageLicenseExpression>
    <PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
    <RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP</RepositoryUrl>
    <PackageProjectUrl>https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP</PackageProjectUrl>
    <RepositoryType>git</RepositoryType>

    <!-- ===== Source-only levers ===== -->
    <!-- 1) Do not ship the compiled DLL; the consumer compiles our source against their GodotSharp. -->
    <IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
    <!-- NU5128: source-only package (dependencies but no lib/ref) — expected, silence it.
         NU1504: Godot.SourceGenerators is re-stated PrivateAssets=all to keep it out of deps (see below). -->
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU5128;NU1504</NoWarn>
    <NoPackageAnalysis>true</NoPackageAnalysis>
    <!-- We hand-pick exactly which files ship (below); turn off default None globbing to avoid duplicates. -->
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
    <!-- Drop the SDK's implicit GodotSharp/GodotSharpEditor so we can re-add them PrivateAssets=all (a body
         <PackageReference Update> does NOT work — the SDK adds them after the project body is evaluated). -->
    <DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>true</DisableImplicitGodotSharpReferences>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    Package DEPENDENCIES: only the engine-agnostic MCP / reflection / query stack (com.IvanMurzak.Rql is the RQL
    module API: IRqlModule, type adapters). A NuGet Version="x" is a ">= x" floor; the pins EQUAL the core
    Godot-MCP addon's (Godot-MCP.csproj; scripts/extensions.py core_pin_drift fails CI otherwise): a lower
    ReflectorNet than the McpPlugin requires is a NU1605 downgrade, a higher pin cannot restore in a consumer
    pinned to the core. `update-core.ps1` / `update-core.py` keep package, tests and testbed in lockstep.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin" Version="8.14.0-dev.e8985d5" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql" Version="0.3.0-dev.0f1bf94" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    GodotSharp is needed for AUTHORING compile only, NOT as a package dependency (the consumer supplies its
    own, version-matched). PrivateAssets=all stops these flowing into the package's dependency list — this
    is the "no GodotSharp dependency" guarantee, verified by inspecting the generated .nuspec.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharpEditor" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'" />
    <!-- Godot.SourceGenerators has no SDK opt-out property, so re-state it (Include) PrivateAssets=all to
         keep it out of the package deps too. This duplicates the SDK's implicit add -> NU1504 (suppressed
         above). The analyzer still runs locally (PrivateAssets governs only what flows to CONSUMERS). -->
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!--
    What ships in the .nupkg:
      • the .cs SOURCE under `src/` (plain files — NOT contentFiles; injected by the props below),
      • `build/<PackageId>.props` (auto-imported by NuGet in the consumer; does the <Compile> injection),
      • README.md (package page).
    The .cs are <Compile> items in THIS authoring build (Godot.NET.Sdk default glob) so they compile +
    unit-test locally; adding them to <None Pack="true"> just also bundles them into the package.
  -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="Editor/**/*.cs" Pack="true" PackagePath="src/Editor/" />
    <None Include="build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera.props" Pack="true" PackagePath="build/" />
    <None Include="README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/README.md`:

```md
# PhantomCamera Tools

RQL module for the Godot Phantom Camera addon: a phantomcamera source that lists virtual cameras and hosts with their modes by name, and validated SetFollow / SetLookAt calls.

Optional Godot-MCP extension, independently versioned as NuGet package `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera` (1.0.1).
Requires a Godot C# project (4.4.0+) with a core `godot_mcp` addon that has the RQL tools
(`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, the release after 0.28.0).

## Required prerequisite — Phantom Camera (install it yourself)

This extension **does NOT include** the Phantom Camera addon and does not download or vendor it. You must
install Phantom Camera into your own Godot project separately:

- Install **Phantom Camera** from the **Godot Asset Library**, or from
  **https://github.com/ramokz/phantom-camera** (tested against **v0.11.0.2**).
- Enable it under **Project Settings → Plugins**.

Without Phantom Camera installed and enabled, `phantomcamera | select installed hint` reports `false` with an install
hint and the `phantomcamera` lists are empty (by design).

> Phantom Camera is © its authors and distributed under the **MIT License**. This extension is **not
> affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by** the Phantom Camera project — it merely provides an RQL module
> that drives it. See the addon's own repository for its licence and terms.

## Install

```sh
godot-cli install-plugin /path/to/project
godot-cli install-extension com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera /path/to/project
godot-cli build /path/to/project
```

The installer resolves the latest stable version from NuGet; use `--version 1.0.1` to request an exact version.
Packages contain C# source and build props, compiled against the project's own GodotSharp.
Previous NuGet versions remain installable after the repository migration.

## RQL

Since 1.0.0 the extension is an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools. Agents set up and read virtual cameras with the
core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools, and the module's guide is part of the core `godot-rql` skill.
Phantom Camera classes are GDScript `class_name`s (no C# type; `class` shows the native base `Node3D` / `Node2D`), so
the module adds:

- **The `phantomcamera` source**: `installed`, `hint` (how to install the addon when it is missing), and the addon's
  nodes in the edited scene as **read-only rows**: `phantomcamera.cameras` (`name path scriptClass priority followMode
  followTarget lookAtMode lookAtTarget followDamping lookAtDamping node`, modes by name) and `phantomcamera.hosts`
  (`name path camera node`).
- **Writes go through the row's `node`** (`get node | set props["priority"] = 50`): the core's writes, undoable, mark
  the scene unsaved. Cameras, hosts and the Camera3D are created with the core `AddChild`.
- **Validated mode calls** on a camera row: `SetFollow(mode, target?)` and `SetLookAt(mode, target?)` take the mode by
  name and set the target after it (the addon silently ignores a target set while the mode is None). An unknown
  mode, ThirdPerson / look-at on a PhantomCamera2D, a single target for None / Group, or a target of the wrong
  dimension fails and changes nothing. They are calls on the row, not on the node, so they are **not undoable** (they
  mark the scene unsaved themselves); the undoable alternative is `get node | set props["follow_mode"] = 2, …`.

```
phantomcamera | select installed hint
root | call AddChild("Camera3D", "Camera3D")
godot.find("Camera3D") | call AddChild("PhantomCameraHost", "PhantomCameraHost")
root | call AddChild("Node3D", "Player")
root | call AddChild("PhantomCamera3D", "PCam")
phantomcamera.cameras | where name == "PCam" | call SetFollow("Simple", "Player")
phantomcamera.cameras | where name == "PCam" | call SetLookAt("Simple", "Player")
phantomcamera.cameras | where name == "PCam" | get node | set props["priority"] = 50, props["follow_damping"] = true
phantomcamera.cameras | select name scriptClass priority followMode followTarget lookAtMode lookAtTarget followDamping
phantomcamera.hosts | select name path camera
```

Without the addon the module still loads: `phantomcamera | select installed hint` returns `false` and the install
hint, and the lists are empty. Save the scene with `editor | call SaveScene()`.

### Migrating from 0.x

| 0.x tool | RQL |
| --- | --- |
| `phantomcamera-defaults` | removed: the guide lists typical values (priority 10, follow / look-at mode Simple, damping on) |
| `phantomcamera-host-create` | `rql-mutate` `root \| call AddChild("Camera3D", "Camera3D")`, then `godot.find("Camera3D") \| call AddChild("PhantomCameraHost", "PhantomCameraHost")` |
| `phantomcamera-create` | `rql-mutate` `root \| call AddChild("PhantomCamera3D", "PCam")`, then `… \| get node \| set props["priority"] = 20` |
| `phantomcamera-set-follow` | `rql-mutate` `phantomcamera.cameras \| where name == "PCam" \| call SetFollow("Simple", "Player")` |
| `phantomcamera-set-look-at` | `rql-mutate` `phantomcamera.cameras \| where name == "PCam" \| call SetLookAt("Simple", "Player")` |
| `phantomcamera-set-priority` | `rql-mutate` `phantomcamera.cameras \| where name == "PCam" \| get node \| set props["priority"] = 50` |
| `phantomcamera-get` | `rql-query` `phantomcamera.cameras \| select name priority followMode followTarget lookAtMode lookAtTarget` |
| `Installed: false` results | `phantomcamera \| select installed hint` |

## Development and releases

See the [monorepo test and release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md).
This module retains its own package, version, tests and Apache-2.0 [license](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/LICENSE).
Releasing another module does not rebuild or republish this package.

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/src/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera.props`:

```props
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  SOURCE INJECTION — the consumer half of the source-only package recipe.                       │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  NuGet auto-imports `build/<PackageId>.props` into any project that references this package. This file
  MUST be named exactly `<PackageId>.props` (com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera.props) or NuGet will
  not import it. `bump-version` / `init` keep the name in lockstep with <PackageId>.

  It adds this package's packed `.cs` (which sit in the NuGet cache under `<package>/<version>/src/`) as
  <Compile> items in the CONSUMER's project, so they compile INSIDE the consumer's Godot project against
  the consumer's own GodotSharp. Because the consumer is a `Godot.NET.Sdk` project, `Godot` types resolve
  and `#if TOOLS` is defined for the editor build — exactly as if the source lived in the consumer's repo.

  • $(MSBuildThisFileDirectory) resolves to `<package>/<version>/build/` in the NuGet cache, so
    `../src/**/*.cs` is the packed source.
  • Exclude="@(Compile)" is belt-and-suspenders against double-inclusion (the consumer's own default
    glob never reaches the NuGet cache, so it normally excludes nothing).
  • Link groups the injected files under the package id in IDEs (cosmetic).
-->
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\src\**\*.cs"
             Exclude="@(Compile)"
             Link="com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera\%(RecursiveDir)%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

`extensions/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera/tests/Godot-AI-PhantomCamera.Tests/PhantomCameraModuleTests.cs`:

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │
│  See the LICENSE file in the project root for more information.  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
*/
#nullable enable
using System.Linq;
using Godot;
using Rql.Execution;
using Xunit;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera.Tests
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The module configures cleanly (without the addon and without Godot) and shapes its view types: the
    /// <c>phantomcamera</c> source, its guide, read-only rows that hold the node, and the validated mode calls. Metadata
    /// only: no member that touches Godot is read.
    /// </summary>
    public class PhantomCameraModuleTests
    {
        private static RqlEngine Engine()
        {
            var engine = new RqlEngine();
            var reports = engine.AddModulesFrom(new[] { typeof(PhantomCameraModule).Assembly });
            Assert.All(reports, r => Assert.True(r.Ok, r.ToString()));
            Assert.Contains(reports, r => r.Module == typeof(PhantomCameraModule).FullName);
            return engine;
        }

        [Fact]
        public void ModuleRegistersItsSourceAndGuide()
        {
            var engine = Engine();
            Assert.True(engine.Sources.ContainsKey("phantomcamera"));
            var guide = Assert.Single(engine.Guides, g => g.Key == PhantomCameraGuide.Topic);
            Assert.Equal(PhantomCameraGuide.Markdown, guide.Value);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TheSourceHasInstalledHintAndTheRowLists()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(PhantomCameraApi));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "installed", "hint", "cameras", "hosts" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void CameraRowsAreReadOnlyWithValidatedModeCalls()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(PhantomCameraRow));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "name", "path", "scriptClass", "priority", "followMode", "followTarget", "lookAtMode", "lookAtTarget", "followDamping", "lookAtDamping", "node" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
            Assert.Equal(typeof(Node), info.Members.Single(m => m.Name == "node").Type);
            foreach (var call in new[] { "SetFollow", "SetLookAt" })
            {
                var method = Assert.Single(info.Callable, c => c.Name == call);
                Assert.Equal(2, method.Parameters.Count);
                Assert.False(method.Parameters[0].HasDefault);
                Assert.True(method.Parameters[1].HasDefault); // the target is optional
            }
        }

        [Fact]
        public void HostRowsAreReadOnly()
        {
            var info = Engine().Types.Info(typeof(PhantomCameraHostRow));
            foreach (var name in new[] { "name", "path", "scriptClass", "camera", "node" })
                Assert.Contains(info.Members, m => m.Name == name && !m.CanWrite);
        }
    }
}

```cs
/*
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Author: Ivan Murzak (https://github.com/IvanMurzak)             │
│  Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak                                  │
│  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.                 │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

#nullable enable
using Xunit;

namespace com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.PhantomCamera.Tests
{
    public class PhantomCameraRulesTests
    {
        [Theory]
        [InlineData("None", PhantomFollowMode.None)]
        [InlineData("simple", PhantomFollowMode.Simple)]
        [InlineData(" GLUED ", PhantomFollowMode.Glued)]
        [InlineData("Framed", PhantomFollowMode.Framed)]
        [InlineData("Third Person", PhantomFollowMode.ThirdPerson)]
        [InlineData("third_person", PhantomFollowMode.ThirdPerson)]
        [InlineData("ThirdPerson", PhantomFollowMode.ThirdPerson)]
        public void FollowModesParseByName(string name, PhantomFollowMode expected)
        {
            Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode(name, is2D: false, out var mode));
            Assert.Equal(expected, mode);
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData("Sideways")]
        [InlineData("")]
        [InlineData(null)]
        [InlineData("2")] // names only: the int values belong to props["follow_mode"]
        public void UnknownFollowModesAreRejected(string? name) =>
            Assert.StartsWith("unknown follow mode", PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode(name, is2D: false, out _));

        [Fact]
        public void ThirdPersonIsA3DMode()
        {
            Assert.Contains("PhantomCamera3D follow mode", PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode("ThirdPerson", is2D: true, out _));
            Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode("Framed", is2D: true, out _));
            Assert.DoesNotContain("ThirdPerson", PhantomCameraRules.FollowMode("x", is2D: true, out _));
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData("Mimic", PhantomLookAtMode.Mimic)]
        [InlineData("group", PhantomLookAtMode.Group)]
        public void LookAtModesParseByName(string name, PhantomLookAtMode expected)
        {
            Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.LookAtMode(name, is2D: false, out var mode));
            Assert.Equal(expected, mode);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void LookAtIsRejectedForUnknownModesAnd2DCameras()
        {
            Assert.StartsWith("unknown look-at mode", PhantomCameraRules.LookAtMode("Glued", is2D: false, out _));
            Assert.Contains("no look-at mode", PhantomCameraRules.LookAtMode("Simple", is2D: true, out _));
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(PhantomFollowMode.Glued)]
        [InlineData(PhantomFollowMode.Simple)]
        [InlineData(PhantomFollowMode.Path)]
        [InlineData(PhantomFollowMode.Framed)]
        [InlineData(PhantomFollowMode.ThirdPerson)]
        public void SingleTargetModesTakeATarget(PhantomFollowMode mode) => Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.FollowTarget(mode));

        [Fact]
        public void NoneAndGroupRejectASingleTarget()
        {
            Assert.Contains("follows nothing", PhantomCameraRules.FollowTarget(PhantomFollowMode.None));
            Assert.Contains("follow_targets", PhantomCameraRules.FollowTarget(PhantomFollowMode.Group));
            Assert.Contains("looks at nothing", PhantomCameraRules.LookAtTarget(PhantomLookAtMode.None));
            Assert.Contains("look_at_targets", PhantomCameraRules.LookAtTarget(PhantomLookAtMode.Group));
            Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.LookAtTarget(PhantomLookAtMode.Mimic));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void TargetsMustMatchTheCameraDimension()
        {
            Assert.Null(PhantomCameraRules.TargetType(false, true, "Player", "Node3D"));
            Assert.Equal("target 'Hud' is a Control; a PhantomCamera3D needs a Node3D", PhantomCameraRules.TargetType(false, false, "Hud", "Control"));
            Assert.Contains("PhantomCamera2D needs a Node2D", PhantomCameraRules.TargetType(true, false, "Player", "Node3D"));
        }

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(0, "None")]
        [InlineData(2, "Simple")]
        [InlineData(6, "ThirdPerson")]
        [InlineData(9, "9")]
        public void FollowLabels(int value, string label) => Assert.Equal(label, PhantomCameraModes.Label<PhantomFollowMode>(value));

        [Theory]
        [InlineData(1, "Mimic")]
        [InlineData(3, "Group")]
        [InlineData(-1, "-1")]
        public void LookAtLabels(int value, string label) => Assert.Equal(label, PhantomCameraModes.Label<PhantomLookAtMode>(value));

        [Fact]
        public void TheInstallHintNamesTheAddonAndItsAutoload()
        {
            Assert.Contains("ramokz/phantom-camera v0.11.0.2", PhantomCameraNames.InstallHint);
            Assert.Contains("PhantomCameraManager", PhantomCameraNames.InstallHint);
        }
    }
}

`extensions/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# AGENTS.md — Godot-AI-Terrain3D

A **Godot-MCP extension** for the third-party [**Terrain3D**](https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D) GDExtension
addon, shipped as an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools, only what the core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` /
`rql-schema` tools need to work with terrains (the `terrain3d` / `terrain3d.addon` sources, the
`terrain3d.newMaterial()` function, `ChangeRegionSize`, an agent guide rendered into the core `godot-rql` skill). A
**source-only NuGet package** (`com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Terrain3D`) compiled inside the consumer's Godot project
against the consumer's own GodotSharp; the packaging recipe is in `docs/source-only-nuget-recipe.md`.

## Layout

- `src/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/Editor/Rql/` — the module:
  - `Terrain3DModule.cs` — the `IRqlModule` (Order 100, `#if TOOLS`): sources, function, guide.
  - `Terrain3DApi.cs` (the sources and the function; `Terrain3DAddon`) and `Terrain3DView.cs` (one row per terrain:
    read-only members, `node`, `ChangeRegionSize`) — `#if TOOLS`.
  - `Terrain3DNames.cs` (the addon's class / snake_case names, region sizes, install hint), `Terrain3DRules.cs`
    (validation) and `Terrain3DGuide.cs` (the guide) — pure-managed, NOT behind `#if TOOLS`.
- `src/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/build/com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Terrain3D.props` — source-injection props, auto-imported by
  NuGet in the consumer; MUST stay named `<PackageId>.props`.
- `tests/Godot-AI-Terrain3D.Tests/` — xUnit (no Godot binary, no addon): rules, names, guide examples parse, the
  module's registrations and view type, and the e2e manifest runs every guide example.
- `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` — the live calls (`rql-*`), driven by `scripts/extension_e2e.py` from the monorepo suite with
  the pinned addon installed (`extension.json` `testAddon`: `TokisanGames/Terrain3D` @ `v1.0.2-stable`).
- `testbed/Terrain3D-Testbed.csproj` — consumer project restoring the local-packed package (injection proof).
- `commands/` — `bump-version`, `update-core`, `init` (`.ps1` + `.py`), `get-version.ps1`.
- CI and publishing are centralized in the monorepo; see `../../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md`.

## Critical invariants (addon-dependent)

- **No compile-time dependency on the addon.** Terrain3D classes have no C# type (a Terrain3D node is a `Node3D`
  wrapper, a Terrain3DMaterial a `Resource`), so adapters cannot target them: reach them by ClassDB name and
  snake_case property / method names from `Terrain3DNames` only. `dotnet build` must pass with the addon absent.
  The addon is never vendored or downloaded by this repo.
- **One approach:** the `terrain3d` source yields read-only `Terrain3DView` rows; writes go to the node itself
  (`get node | set props["…"]`), so they are undoable through the core hooks. Only `ChangeRegionSize` is a view
  call: it validates the size (Terrain3D logs an error for any other value), is not undoable (the size is not a
  stored scene property) and marks the scene unsaved itself.
- **Missing addon:** `terrain3d` is empty, `terrain3d.addon` reports `installed: false` plus the install hint,
  `terrain3d.newMaterial()` fails with that hint — never a crash.
- Every guide example runs, in order, in `tests/e2e/e2e-tools.json` (xUnit-asserted). The module uses only Godot,
  `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` and the BCL, never core-addon types.

## Build / test (no Godot binary, addon absent)

```bash
dotnet build src/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/Godot-AI-Terrain3D.csproj -c Debug   # the module (#if TOOLS included)
dotnet test  tests/Godot-AI-Terrain3D.Tests/Godot-AI-Terrain3D.Tests.csproj
```

The live suite (one headless editor for every module) is `python scripts/test_extensions.py` from the monorepo
root. `dotnet pack` reuses the **global NuGet cache** for an already-cached version: when re-packing the same
`Version`, clear `~/.nuget/packages/com.ivanmurzak.godot.mcp.terrain3d/<ver>` (or pack a unique version).

## Conventions

- Root namespace `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Terrain3D`. It contains `com.IvanMurzak.Godot`, so an inline
  `Godot.`-qualified type binds to that ancestor: write `global::Godot.…` or rely on `using Godot;`. Every `.cs`
  starts with the Apache-2.0 header and `#nullable enable`.
- The package declares only the `com.IvanMurzak.McpPlugin` / `ReflectorNet` / `Rql` pins (equal to the core's); **GodotSharp and the
  Terrain3D addon must never become package dependencies** (CI asserts the nuspec). Bump them with
  `commands/update-core.ps1`.

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/README.md`:

```md
# Terrain3D Tools

RQL module for the Terrain3D addon (TokisanGames heightmap terrain): terrain3d source with validated ChangeRegionSize, addon check and material creation for the core rql-query / rql-mutate tools, plus an agent guide.

Optional Godot-MCP extension, independently versioned as NuGet package `com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Terrain3D` (1.0.1).
Requires a Godot C# project (4.4.0+) with a core `godot_mcp` addon that has the RQL tools
(`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, the release after 0.28.0).

## Required prerequisite — Terrain3D (install it yourself)

This extension **does NOT include** the Terrain3D addon and does not download or vendor it. You must
install Terrain3D into your own Godot project separately:

- Install **Terrain3D** from the **Godot Asset Library** (search "Terrain3D"), or from
  **https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D** (tested against **v1.0.2-stable**). Terrain3D ships
  **precompiled binaries** in its release — no C++ build is required.
- Unzip it into **`addons/terrain_3d/`**, **restart Godot** (a GDExtension only loads on editor
  startup), then enable it under **Project Settings → Plugins**.

Without Terrain3D installed and enabled, the `terrain3d` source is empty and `terrain3d.addon | select installed hint`
says how to install it (by design).

> Terrain3D is © its authors and distributed under the **MIT License**. This extension is
> **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by** the Terrain3D project — it merely provides AI
> tools that drive it. See the addon's own repository for its licence and terms.

## Install

```sh
godot-cli install-plugin /path/to/project
godot-cli install-extension com.IvanMurzak.Godot.MCP.Terrain3D /path/to/project
godot-cli build /path/to/project
```

The installer resolves the latest stable version from NuGet; use `--version 1.0.1` to request an exact version.
Packages contain C# source and build props, compiled against the project's own GodotSharp.
Previous NuGet versions remain installable after the repository migration.

## RQL

Since 1.0.0 the extension is an **RQL module**: it adds no MCP tools. Agents create, configure and read terrains
with the core `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools, and the module's guide is part of the core
`godot-rql` skill. Terrain3D is a GDExtension class without a C# type (its nodes are `Node3D` in RQL, `class ==
"Terrain3D"`), so the module adds sources and a function rather than adapters:

- **`terrain3d`**: one row per Terrain3D node of the edited scene, with `node`, `name`, `path`, `regionSize`,
  `dataDirectory`, `material`, `regionCount`, `meshLods`, `meshSize`, `vertexSpacing`, `version`, and
  **`ChangeRegionSize(size)`** (64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048; any other size fails and changes nothing, 0.x
  snapped it; not undoable, the size lives in the region data).
- **`terrain3d.addon`**: `installed` / `hint`, whether the Terrain3D GDExtension is loaded.
- **`terrain3d.newMaterial()`**: a new Terrain3DMaterial (made through ClassDB) to assign to a terrain.

Write a terrain's properties on its node (`get node | set props["…"] = …`): those writes are undoable and mark
the scene unsaved (`editor | call SaveScene()` writes it, and Terrain3D saves its regions to `data_directory`).

```
terrain3d.addon | select installed hint
root | call AddChild("Terrain3D", "Terrain")
terrain3d | select name regionSize dataDirectory meshLods meshSize vertexSpacing version
terrain3d | where name == "Terrain" | call ChangeRegionSize(1024)
terrain3d | where name == "Terrain" | get node | set props["data_directory"] = "res://terrain_data"
terrain3d | where name == "Terrain" | get node | set props["material"] = terrain3d.newMaterial()
terrain3d | where name == "Terrain" | get node | set props["mesh_lods"] = 8, props["vertex_spacing"] = 2
terrain3d | select name regionSize dataDirectory material.class regionCount meshLods vertexSpacing
```

### Migrating from 0.x

| 0.x tool | RQL |
| --- | --- |
| `terrain3d-defaults` | removed: typical values (region size 256 to 1024, `mesh_lods` 7, `mesh_size` 48, `vertex_spacing` 1, `res://terrain_data`) are in the guide |
| `terrain3d-create` | `rql-mutate` `root \| call AddChild("Terrain3D", "Terrain")`, then `call ChangeRegionSize(…)` / `set props["data_directory"] = …` |
| `terrain3d-set-data-directory` | `rql-mutate` `terrain3d \| where name == "Terrain" \| get node \| set props["data_directory"] = "res://terrain_data"` |
| `terrain3d-set-region-size` | `rql-mutate` `terrain3d \| where name == "Terrain" \| call ChangeRegionSize(512)` (an exact size: no more snapping) |
| `terrain3d-set-material` | `rql-mutate` `terrain3d \| where name == "Terrain" \| get node \| set props["material"] = terrain3d.newMaterial()` |
| `terrain3d-get` | `rql-query` `terrain3d \| select name regionSize dataDirectory material.class regionCount version`; addon presence: `terrain3d.addon \| select installed hint` |

## Development and releases

See the [monorepo test and release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md).
This module retains its own package, version, tests and Apache-2.0 [license](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/extensions/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/LICENSE).
Releasing another module does not rebuild or republish this package.

## Asset Library installation

The independent Asset Library entry is named **Godot MCP - Terrain3D** and becomes public after moderator approval.
It downloads only this extension from its versioned GitHub release. Install Godot MCP core
and configure its NuGet dependencies first, then install the archive into the project and build C#.
The archive includes its own license, README and installation instructions. Third-party addon
prerequisites listed above still apply. Use either this source installation or this extension
NuGet package in a project; installing both creates duplicate C# types.

See the [Asset Library release guide](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md#godot-asset-library).

`extensions/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/commands/bump-version.ps1`:

```ps1
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Set the extension package version (the single source of truth: the package csproj <Version>).

.DESCRIPTION
    Updates <Version> in the source-only package csproj under src/. The release workflow is version-gated
    on this value (it publishes only when <Version> increases AND the tag does not yet exist).

.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/bump-version.ps1 -NewVersion "1.0.1"
.EXAMPLE
    ./commands/bump-version.ps1 -NewVersion "1.0.1" -WhatIf
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$NewVersion,
    [switch]$WhatIf
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "../extension.json")) {
    $pythonCommand = Get-Command py, python3, python -CommandType Application -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $pythonCommand) { throw "Python 3 is required for the central version helper." }
    $pythonArguments = @()
    if ($pythonCommand.Name -match '^py(\.exe)?$') { $pythonArguments += '-3' }
    $pythonArguments += @((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "bump-version.py"), $NewVersion)
    if ($WhatIf) { $pythonArguments += '--what-if' }
    & $pythonCommand.Source @pythonArguments
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

if ($NewVersion -notmatch '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z\.\-]+)?$') {
    throw "Invalid semantic version: '$NewVersion' (expected major.minor.patch[-prerelease])."
}

$RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$csproj = Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $RepoRoot "src") -Recurse -Filter *.csproj |
    Where-Object { (Get-Content $_.FullName -Raw) -match '<PackageId>' } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $csproj) { throw "Could not find the package csproj (with <PackageId>) under src/." }

$content = Get-Content $csproj.FullName -Raw
if ($content -notmatch '<Version>([^<]+)</Version>') { throw "No <Version> element in $($csproj.Name)." }
$current = $Matches[1]
$new = $content -replace '<Version>[^<]+</Version>', "<Version>$NewVersion</Version>"

Write-Host "Package: $($csproj.Name)"
Write-Host "Version: $current -> $NewVersion"
if ($WhatIf) { Write-Host "(WhatIf — no changes written)" -ForegroundColor Yellow; exit 0 }
Set-Content -Path $csproj.FullName -Value $new -NoNewline
Write-Host "Updated." -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Remember to commit, then push to main to trigger the version-gated release."

```

`extensions/Godot-AI-Terrain3D/commands/bump-version.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Set the extension package version (the package csproj <Version>). POSIX/Python mirror of bump-version.ps1.

Usage:
  python commands/bump-version.py 1.0.1
  python commands/bump-version.py 1.0.1 --what-if
  python commands/bump-version.py --get        # print current version
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SEMVER = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.\-]+)?$")


def find_package_csproj(root: Path) -> Path:
    for p in (root / "src").rglob("*.csproj"):
        if "<PackageId>" in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
            return p
    raise SystemExit("error: could not find the package csproj (with <PackageId>) under src/")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("version", nargs="?", help="new semantic version, e.g. 1.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--what-if", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--get", action="store_true", help="print current version and exit")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    if (root / "extension.json").is_file():
        # Keep the monorepo inventory and package README versions in sync.
        sys.path.insert(0, str(root.parents[1] / "scripts"))
        from extension_release import bump
        from extensions import modules, SEMVER as stable_version
        module = modules(only=[root.name])[0]
        if args.get:
            print(module["version"])
            return 0
        if not args.version or not stable_version.fullmatch(args.version):
            ap.error("pass a stable major.minor.patch version")
        if args.what_if:
            print(f"{module['name']}: {module['version']} -> {args.version} (what-if)")
            return 0
        bump(module, args.version)
        return 0
    csproj = find_package_csproj(root)
    content = csproj.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r"<Version>([^<]+)</Version>", content)
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"error: no <Version> element in {csproj.name}")
    current = m.group(1)

    if args.get:
        print(current)
        return 0

    if not args.version or not SEMVER.match(args.version):
        print("error: pass a semantic version major.minor.patch[-prerelease]", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    print(f"Package: {csproj.name}")
    print(f"Version: {current} -> {args.version}")
    if args.what_if:
        print("(what-if — no changes written)")
        return 0
    csproj.write_text(re.sub(r"<Version>[^<]+</Version>", f"<Version>{args.version}</Version>", content),
                       encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    print("Updated.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

# Print the extension package version (the package csproj <Version>). Used by CI's version gate.
